## 2026-10-23 — Stage 16e: Account Page (`/account`)

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-sonnet-5)
**Mode:** generate, debug
**Scope:** Implementation code, Debugging
**Governing decision:** instructions.md Stage 16e (the account-page spec) and its Stage 16 decisions table; user-service's `me.controller.ts`/`me.service.ts` for the exact request/response shapes and error codes of each `/users/me/*` endpoint

**Prompts (exact):**

> done, go for hte next part

**Key responses:**
Pulled `main` first (fast-forwarded past the already-merged Stage 16d PR #131) and branched `feat/stage-16e-account-page` from it, per the team's standing git workflow.

Read `user-service/src/controllers/me.controller.ts` and `me.service.ts` to pin down each endpoint exactly: `PUT /users/me/username` returns `{username, email}` and can throw `USERNAME_UNCHANGED`/`USERNAME_TAKEN`; `PUT /users/me/email` only sends an OTP (`EMAIL_UNCHANGED`/`EMAIL_TAKEN`/`INVALID_PASSWORD`), confirmed via `POST /users/me/verify-otp` (`purpose: 'change_email'` — the only purpose that route accepts); `PUT /users/me/password` similarly only sends an OTP (`PASSWORD_UNCHANGED`/`INVALID_PASSWORD`), confirmed via `POST /users/me/confirm-password-change`, which also re-validates `PASSWORD_UNCHANGED` and can still throw `INVALID_OTP`/`OTP_EXPIRED`/`OTP_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED` (traced into `otp.service.ts`'s `checkOtp`, the single place all three of those actually originate); the one `POST /users/me/resend-otp` route takes either purpose.

Created `src/pages/Account.jsx`: a profile section plus three independent change sections (username, email, password), each its own local sub-component with its own form/OTP state. Username is a single-step form. Email and password are two-step within their own section (form, then an inline OTP step), matching the spec's "OTP shown inline in the same section." Password's new value is kept in the section's own state from the first step through to `confirm-password-change`, per the spec, so the user isn't asked to retype it.

Extended `src/api/profile.js` with `changeUsername`, `changeEmail`, `verifyEmailChangeOtp`, `resendMeOtp`, `changePassword`, `confirmPasswordChange` — thin wrappers over `request()`. Added `src/context/AuthContext.jsx`'s `forceReauth(message)` for the spec's forced-relogin decision (clears client state the same way `logout()` does, without the `POST /auth/logout` call, since the backend has already revoked every refresh token for this user). Wired `/account` into `App.jsx` behind `RequireAuth`, and linked it from the nav by turning `TopNav.jsx`'s existing username/initials block (desktop and mobile) into a link to `/account`, since that was the only place already identifying the signed-in user — kept `TopNav.jsx` changes to just that.

**A real bug, found only by actually running the password-change flow, not by reasoning about the code:** the spec's forced-relogin banner never appeared. Root-caused with Playwright plus console tracing (see `AuthContext.jsx`'s comment on `forceReauth` for the full trail): flipping auth state to anonymous from `/account` (a `RequireAuth`-protected route) makes `RequireAuth` re-render and fire its _own_ redirect to `/login`, racing `forceReauth`'s intended navigation for who gets to set the router state `/login` reads the banner text from. React Router v7 schedules a plain `navigate()`'s location update inside `React.startTransition` by default, so `RequireAuth`'s synchronous re-render (triggered by the plain `setUser`/`setStatus` calls) consistently won before this call's location update had landed — confirmed by tracing actual render order with temporary logging, not just reading the types. Tried three fixes in order before one worked: reordering the calls (no effect), wrapping the call in React DOM's own `flushSync` (no effect — react-router's internal `startTransition` isn't overridden by an outer `flushSync` boundary), and react-router v7's own `navigate(..., { flushSync: true })` option (still no effect, empirically — plausibly because this project uses the plain `<BrowserRouter>` API, not the data-router `RouterProvider` that option targets). Settled on sidestepping the race entirely: the message now travels through a small module-level variable in `AuthContext.jsx` (`pendingAuthMessage`/`consumePendingAuthMessage`/`clearPendingAuthMessage`) instead of router state, so it no longer matters which navigate call's state wins — `Login.jsx` reads it once via a pure lazy `useState` initializer (safe under StrictMode's double-invoked renders, since a plain read has no side effect) and clears it in a separate effect (idempotent, so a StrictMode double-invoked effect is harmless too).

Verified: `npm run build` and `npm run lint` clean (the two new `only-export-components` warnings for the module-level pending-message functions are the same pre-existing category already present elsewhere in this codebase — `Toast.jsx`, `ApiNotice.jsx`, `DemoContext.jsx` — not a new kind of finding). Ran Playwright (headless Chromium, real Docker stack) end to end: the nav link reaches `/account`; profile shows the signed-in user's username/email; changing to the current username shows `USERNAME_UNCHANGED` inline; changing it for real updates the section, a success banner, and the nav's displayed name with no reload; the email section's wrong-password case shows `INVALID_PASSWORD` inline on the password field; the happy path sends an OTP (read from the user-service dev-console log), a wrong code shows "That code is incorrect.", and the right code updates the profile's email with no reload; the password section's happy path sends an OTP, and entering the right code immediately redirects to `/login` with "Password changed. Please sign in again with your new password." — not left on `/account`; the old password then fails login and the new one succeeds.

Read `user-service/src/routes/users.routes.ts`, `users.controller.ts` and `users.service.ts` to pin down the exact backend behaviour the row-actions menu needs to mirror: `GET /users` (admin+) takes `page/username/email/status/role/sortBy/sortDir`, defaults `sortBy` to `createdAt` and `sortDir` to `desc` when unset; `PUT /:id/status` (admin+) throws `SUPER_ADMIN_IMMUTABLE` (403) on a super-admin target, `FORBIDDEN` (403) when an admin targets another admin, and `CANNOT_CHANGE_STATUS_PENDING_USER` (422) on a pending target; `PUT /:id/role` (super admin only) throws `SELF_ROLE_CHANGE` (403) on the caller's own id, `SUPER_ADMIN_IMMUTABLE` (403) on a super-admin target, and `CANNOT_CHANGE_ROLE_PENDING_USER`/`CANNOT_CHANGE_ROLE_SUSPENDED_USER` (422) depending on target status. Wrote `getRowActions(viewer, row)` in `AdminUsers.jsx` as a direct, side-by-side translation of those backend checks (own row / super-admin target / pending target → no menu at all; suspend shown for a super-admin viewer on any user-or-admin row, or an admin viewer only on a user-role row; promote/demote shown only for a super-admin viewer on an active row, promote if the target is `user`, demote if `admin`) — this is the single source the row menu, and nothing else, decides visibility from.

Created `src/api/users.js` (`listUsers`, `updateUserStatus`, `updateUserRole`) and `src/pages/AdminUsers.jsx`: debounced (300ms, independent timers) username/email search boxes, status/role filter selects, click-to-sort username/email/created headers (status/role are not sortable, per spec), the existing `Pager`/`useApiNotice` components reused from `ApiNotice.jsx` (mapping its `metadata.currPage` naming onto the user-service response's `page` field), a three-dot row menu (visible on hover at `sm`+, always visible below it, closes on outside click), and a confirmation dialog reusing `AdminSuppliers.jsx`'s `DeleteDialog` visual pattern. Declined to import `AdminSuppliers.jsx`'s exported `selectClass` constant or its `Badge` component to avoid a styling dependency between the two unrelated admin screens; duplicated the (short) class strings locally instead. Wired `/admin/users` into `App.jsx` behind `RequireAuth` + `RequireRole minimum="admin"` (both nested, matching the stage text verbatim, even though `RequireRole` alone already re-implements the auth check).

Verified: `npm run build` and `npm run lint` (oxlint) clean, no new warnings beyond the same `set-state-in-effect` category already present on `AdminSuppliers.jsx`'s identical page-reset effect. Ran the app against the real Docker stack with a headless Playwright/Chromium script driving three separate logged-in sessions (super admin, a promoted admin account, and a plain user), registering throwaway test users via the API and reading their OTPs from the user-service dev-console log: confirmed username-substring search, the pending-status filter, and username sort all changed the request/results; a pending row showed no menu; a super-admin viewer saw Suspend+Promote on an active plain user and Suspend+Demote on an active admin; promoting and suspending both updated the row in place and showed a success toast (confirmed by DB: suspending an admin revoked their refresh token in the same transaction, as Stage 9/10 already guaranteed); an admin viewer saw Unsuspend on a suspended plain user but no menu at all on another admin's row or their own row; a plain user hitting `/admin/users` directly got the "Not authorised" view with the URL unchanged and no "Manage users" nav link. Did not exercise the multi-page Pager path (only a handful of test users existed, so `totalPages` was always 1) — `Pager` itself is the same already-verified component `AdminSuppliers.jsx` uses, unchanged here.

If it isn't fixed by tomorrow, add it to the exclusion with the same style of comment, since a job that's red one run in four will train everyone to ignore CI.

**Key responses:**

_Derived, not guessed._ Both Postgres service containers were read off the suites that use them. `user-service/tests/setup/globalSetup.ts` connects to the `postgres` maintenance database as `DB_USER`/`DB_PASSWORD`, drops and recreates `DB_NAME`, then applies `src/db/init.sql`; the committed `.env.test` fixes those to postgres/postgres on port 5434. `credit-service`'s does the same and then creates the least-privilege role and applies `grants.sql` with `credit_app` rewritten to the test role, so the suite runs under the same privileges as production (NFR8.2.3) — which is why CI needs no separate grants step. Neither needs the gitignored RS256 keypair: both generate a throwaway pair at run time.

_Fix 3 turned out to be unnecessary._ `src/generated/` is already in `order-service/.gitignore` line 7. The earlier audit reported otherwise because `git check-ignore` was called on the path without a trailing slash while the directory did not exist, so the directory-only pattern did not match. No change made.

_Fix 1 had an interaction worth recording._ The Dockerfile's `deps` stage runs `npm ci` with only `package.json` and the lockfile copied, before the source arrives, so a plain `postinstall: prisma generate` would have broken the image build. The script skips when `prisma/schema.prisma` is absent; the `build` stage still generates explicitly once the source is there.

_Fix 2 was a real latent break, not just a host artefact._ `@types/node@^20` against `vitest@5`'s peerOptional of `^22 || >=24` resolves on npm 11.19.1 and aborts on 11.6.2. The lockfile was regenerated inside `node:24-alpine` so the diff is the two packages that changed rather than 36 lines of unrelated `"peer": true` churn a different npm emits.

**Verification actually run** — each job's sequence, with `node_modules` deleted first:

| Job              | Result                                                        |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| user-service     | **682/682** on Linux Node 24; 667/682 on the Windows host     |
| credit-service   | **123/123**, 13 files                                         |
| order-service    | **613/613**, 14 files                                         |
| supplier-service | **336/336** with the excluded file, but see below             |
| frontend         | lint exit 0 (14 warnings), **build exit 0**, 385.62 kB bundle |

The 15 `user-service` failures on the Windows host are all `tests/config.test.ts`, which `spawnSync`s the extensionless `node_modules/.bin/tsx` shim. Previously asserted to be host-specific; now proven, by running the suite inside `node:24-slim` against the compose-network Postgres: 25 files, 682 tests, zero failures.

For order-service, the brief's two conditions were checked literally: with `node_modules` and `src/generated` deleted and no `DATABASE_URL` in the environment, `npm ci` alone emitted `✔ Generated Prisma Client (7.10.0)`; and the unit suite then passed 613/613 with `DATABASE_URL` pointed at `localhost:59999`.

Also verified rather than assumed: `user-service` and `supplier-service` both use `"test": "vitest"`, which is watch mode and would hang a CI job. Vitest self-detects `CI=true`, which GitHub Actions sets. Confirmed inside `node:24-alpine` that `CI=true npm test -- --exclude test/app.integration.test.ts` runs once and excludes correctly.

**Deviations / questions raised for the team:**

1. **A second, previously unknown flaky test in supplier-service.** `test/middleware/authenticate.test.ts > rejects expired and incorrectly signed tokens` fails intermittently — measured at **2 failures in 8 runs of the real CI command**, while passing 6/6 when that file runs alone. Cause: the test tampers a token with `token({}, kid).replace(/.$/, "x")`, replacing only the final base64url character. A 2048-bit RSA signature base64url-encodes to 342 characters whose last character carries just 2 significant bits, so several substitutions decode to the identical byte sequence and the tampered token still verifies. It is not in the excluded file. Left in at the user's instruction, who is reporting it to supplier-service's owner with the diagnosis; to be added to the exclusion if unfixed by 2026-11-03. The fix is to corrupt a byte in the middle of the signature rather than the last character.
2. **Frontend lint warning count: the "8 → 14 drift" could not be substantiated.** The figure of 8 came from a 2026-10-22 command that piped `npm run lint` through `tail -12`, so it showed the last few warning lines, not a total — there was never a reliable baseline. The current count is **14 (7 × `react(set-state-in-effect)`, 7 × `react(only-export-components)`)**. Frontend did gain seven commits of new pages in between (stages 16b–16g), so growth is plausible, but the delta is not evidence. Recorded so the PR description does not assert a trend that was not measured.
3. **order-service's e2e suite is not covered by CI**, recorded in a comment on the job. Adding it needs a Postgres + Redis service pair and a `prisma migrate deploy` step, which is order-service's owner's call.
4. **Three jobs were verified only on Windows / Node 25**, not Linux / Node 24: credit-service, order-service and supplier-service. user-service was additionally run on Linux Node 24 because that is where the disputed failures were, and frontend only on Linux because the Windows host EPERMs on a rolldown binding held open by a running Vite dev server. The first Actions run is the real check, per the user's instruction not to re-run containerised locally.
5. **`npm run lint` on the frontend stays informational** — no `--max-warnings 0` — by the user's decision, so warnings will not fail the build.

## 2026-11-03 — CI: restore supplier-service's full suite after the JWKS test fixes

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-opus-5)
**Mode:** debug | generate
**Scope:** Implementation code | Debugging
**Governing decision:** The user's instruction of 2026-11-03, quoted below. The supplier-service fixes being verified are `upstream/update-supplier-auth-integration` (commits `00ee616`, `a59cd0c`, `3dd0d58`), authored by that service's owner.

**Prompts (exact):**

> Git work, then verify, then one small CI change.
>
> ## 1. Sync
>
> Report `git status` first — if there's uncommitted work, stop and tell me rather than stashing or committing it.
>
> Then:
>
> - fetch upstream
> - merge upstream/update-supplier-auth-integration into my main
> - report what came with it besides the supplier fixes, since a feature branch may carry unrelated commits
> - create d4-iteration-2 from main and check it out
>
> ## 2. Verify the fixes before trusting them
>
> That branch is meant to fix two things in supplier-service. Confirm both, by reading the diff rather than by a green run:
>
> a. The 5 stale tests in test/app.integration.test.ts. They authenticated with the literal string `Bearer good-token`, which cannot survive RS256 verification since the JWKS migration. Does the fix generate a keypair and sign a real token, the way test/middleware/authenticate.test.ts already does?
>
> b. The flake in test/middleware/authenticate.test.ts > "rejects expired and incorrectly signed tokens". It tampered the token with `.replace(/.$/, "x")` — the last base64url character of a 2048-bit RSA signature carries only two significant bits, so w/x/y/z decode identically and the forged token still verified about one run in four. Does the fix corrupt a byte in the middle of the signature instead? If it still touches the final character, the flake is not fixed regardless of what the suite does today.
>
> Say plainly whether each root cause is addressed. If either isn't, stop before step 3.
>
> ## 3. Restore the test in CI
>
> Only if both check out: remove the TEMPORARY EXCLUSION block and the --exclude flag from the supplier-service job in .github/workflows/ci.yml, so the full suite runs again. Leave the order-service e2e comment where it is.
>
> ## 4. Prove it
>
> Run supplier-service's full suite — no exclusions — at least 15 times in a row and report the pass rate. One green run proves nothing against a 25% flake; I want the count.
>
> Also run the other four jobs' sequences once to confirm the merge didn't break anything else.
>
> Report actual numbers. Commit nothing until I've seen them.

**Key responses:**

_Merge._ The branch carried three commits and nine files; the only ones outside `supplier-service/` were its own `README.md` row and `ai/usage-log.md` entry, so no unrelated feature work rode along. Four conflicts, all resolved deliberately: `supplier-service/package.json` and `package-lock.json` took the branch's `@types/node@^24.19.2` over the `^24.0.0` committed here on 2026-11-02 (same fix, theirs more precise, and it is their service); `README.md` kept both sides' Log index rows with theirs renumbered to 145 and 146; `ai/usage-log.md` kept both entries, since the log is append-only.

_Verification, by reading the diff._ Both root causes are addressed. (a) `app.integration.test.ts` now generates a 2048-bit keypair, serves the matching JWK from the mocked JWKS fetch, and signs real tokens with `createSign('RSA-SHA256')`, matching the pattern `test/middleware/authenticate.test.ts` already used; no `good-token` literal remains anywhere in the test tree. (b) the forged-signature test now decodes the signature to bytes and flips a bit in byte 0 rather than substituting the last base64url character. Worth recording precisely: the fix touches the _first_ byte, not the middle as the brief anticipated, which is immaterial — the defect was never position but that a base64 character's low bits are padding, whereas every bit of a decoded RSA signature is significant.

## 2026-11-04 — Stage 18: Account Lockout and OTP Send Escalation (NFR1.1)

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-sonnet-5)
**Mode:** generate, refactor, debug
**Scope:** Implementation code
**Governing decision:** `instructions.md` Stage 18 (design-decision tables for login lockout,
OTP send escalation, admin unlock, config, and cross-cutting rules — "Every decision in the
table below was made by the team"). The stage's own text was originally pasted into
`ai/usage-log.md` by the user as a scratch draft; at the start of this session it was relocated
into `instructions.md` (pure relocation/formatting, no content authored by the AI) and committed
separately as `d3c7bb6`, per the user's correction below, before any implementation began.

**Prompts (exact):**

> read stage 18. are you ready to impement it?

> oops put it into instructions.md instead. don't forget the git workflow. just do everything in one pass bah

**Key responses:**
Before writing code, confirmed every §2.1 stop-and-ask trigger was already resolved by the
stage's own "already made, do not change" decision tables, so no design/schema/API questions
needed to be raised. Initially proposed the usual per-sub-stage (18a→18f) branch/PR sequence per
the team's standing git workflow, but the user's second prompt asked for everything in one pass
instead, so all of 18a–18f were implemented together against `main`, uncommitted, to be reviewed
and shipped as a single PR rather than six.

Implemented, in order:

- **18a** (schema/config): the four `users` login-lockout columns and two `users_otps`
  send-escalation columns in `init.sql`; `LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES`, `LOGIN_FAILURE_WINDOW_MINUTES`,
  `LOCK_ESCALATION_HOURS`, `LOCK_ESCALATION_RESET_HOURS` added to `config.ts`'s Zod schema and
  to `.env.example`/`.env`/`.env.test`.
- Shared foundation: a new `src/services/lockEscalation.ts` holding the escalation-duration/
  message/quiet-window-reset math used by both the login lock and the OTP send block, so the two
  features (18b, 18c) share one implementation of the "1h → 4h → 24h, resets after 24h quiet"
  rule rather than duplicating it.
- **18b** (login lockout): `recordLoginFailure` and the `login()` flow in `auth.service.ts`
  check the lock before the password check, count failures, lock on threshold, and reset on
  success, skipping `pending`/`suspended` accounts. `me.service.ts`'s
  `initiateEmailChange`/`initiatePasswordChange` reject `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` before the password
  check and feed `INVALID_PASSWORD` into the same counter.
- **18c** (OTP send escalation): `otp.service.ts`'s `requestOtp` applies the escalating block for
  `forgot_password`/`change_email`/`change_password`, writing the new level/block-end onto the
  latest existing row on a cap hit and copying them forward onto each new row; registration left
  unchanged. `forgotPassword`/`resetPassword` (auth.service.ts) and
  `throwOnUnsentOtp`/`verifyEmailChangeOtp`/`confirmPasswordChange` (me.service.ts) get the
  level-matched message and `Retry-After`, and reset the level on a successful consuming verify.
- **18d** (admin): `POST /users/:id/unlock` (route, controller, `users.service.ts`'s
  `unlockUser`) mirroring `changeUserStatus`'s permission rules; `isLocked`/`lockedUntil`/
  `lockLevel` added to `userResponse.ts`; a `locked=true|false` filter added to `listUsersPage`/
  the `GET /users` controller.
- **18e** (frontend): `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` added to `errorMessages.js` as a banner (`Login.jsx`
  already renders any banner-type error generically, so it needed no code change itself);
  `unlockUser` added to `api/users.js`; `AdminUsers.jsx` gained the three lock fields as table
  columns, a `locked` filter, and an Unlock row action gated by the same `getRowActions`-style
  visibility rule as Suspend.
- **Mid-stream refactor:** found that a send-escalation cap hit's write (18c) inside
  `initiateEmailChange`/`initiatePasswordChange`'s transaction was being silently rolled back
  whenever the same call path then threw `OTP_RESEND_LIMIT` or `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` later in the same
  transaction. Fixed by converting `recordLoginFailure` and `throwOnUnsentOtp` from
  throw-on-detection to return-a-result, so the caller can commit the escalation write before
  throwing the corresponding error outside the transaction. This is an implementation-level fix
  for a correctness bug in how the already-decided behaviour was being persisted, not a new
  design decision.
- **18f** (tests): added lockout and OTP-escalation-reset unit/controller tests across
  `auth.service.test.ts`, `auth.controller.test.ts`, `me.service.test.ts`,
  `otp.service.test.ts`, `users.service.test.ts`, `users.controller.test.ts`; added

claims against the current code (all matched exactly). Found one place where the stage's
decision table disagreed with the code: it said to pass username at `forgotPassword()` (line 466) "from the locked row", but `forgotPassword()` has no locked row at that point — only the
unlocked `findByEmail` read (`requestOtp` does its own internal lock later, inside
`otp.service.ts`). Stopped and asked; the user chose to use that unlocked row's username
(`user.username`), not to add a new lock, since the latter would be a new locking decision, not
implementation of an existing one.

Implemented the retry loop, per-attempt cap, backoff, deadline and logging entirely inside
`sendOtpEmail` (`email.service.ts`), per the stage's "retry loop location" decision — its
contract (resolve on success, throw after the final failure) is unchanged, so `issueOtp`'s
try/catch/`AppError(503, ...)` wrapping needed no changes beyond threading `username` through.
Added phase timeouts (`connectionTimeout`/`greetingTimeout`/`socketTimeout`/`dnsTimeout`, all
5000ms) to `createTransport()`. The per-attempt cap races `sendMail()` against a `setTimeout`;
an attempt cut off by the cap is left to settle on its own, with a `settled` flag guarding
`resolve`/`reject` so the eventual result is swallowed (no unhandled rejection, no log line) and
the timer is cleared whenever the send settles first. Error classification
(`isTransientError`/`describeAttemptError`) follows the stage's table exactly: `ETIMEDOUT`/
`ESOCKET`/`ECONNECTION`/`EDNS` always transient; `EENVELOPE`/`EMESSAGE`/`EAUTH` transient only
for `responseCode` 400–499; everything else (including the synthetic `ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT`, which is
always transient) non-transient. Backoff is `Math.random() * Math.min(300, 2**(n-1)) * 1000`ms,
and a wait is skipped (immediate throw instead) if `Date.now() - startedAt + waitMs` would
exceed the 30s deadline. No new env vars; constants are at the top of `email.service.ts` as
specified.

Threaded `username` through `issueOtp`/`requestOtp` (`otp.service.ts`) and all six call sites
across `auth.service.ts` (`register`, `resendRegistrationOtp`, `forgotPassword`) and

responseCode boundary (both sides), the three non-transient "fail immediately" cases, backoff
wait ranges (via fake timers, no real sleeping), the 5s cap cutoff and abandoned-send handling,

user's own spec text, unchanged.

Created `frontend/src/components/ActionMenu.jsx`: a trigger `<button>` (`aria-haspopup="menu"`,
`aria-expanded`, caller-supplied `aria-label` and trigger content) plus a `role="menu"` panel
rendered via `createPortal` into `document.body`. A `useLayoutEffect` (run once per open, after
the portal content commits) measures the trigger and menu with `getBoundingClientRect()` and
sets `position: fixed` coordinates: below the trigger and right-aligned to it with a 4px gap by
default, flipped above the trigger if it would overflow `window.innerHeight - 8px`, with `left`
clamped to a minimum of 8px. The menu stays `visibility: hidden` until a position is computed,
avoiding a flash at `(0, 0)`. A second effect (also keyed on `open`) attaches `mousedown`
(outside-close), `keydown` (Escape — closes and returns focus to the trigger), `resize`, and
`scroll` (capture phase, so a scroll starting on an ancestor like the table wrapper still
closes it) listeners, all removed on close/unmount. Items are `{ label, onSelect, danger? }`;
`danger` reuses the existing `text-alert` destructive colour. Returns `null` when `items` is
empty, matching the old `RowMenu`'s behaviour.

In `frontend/src/pages/AdminUsers.jsx`, replaced `RowMenu`'s inline absolutely-positioned
dropdown (the thing `overflow-x: auto` on the table wrapper was clipping) with `ActionMenu`,
passing through the same `getRowActions`-derived item set, the same per-item handlers via
`onPick`, and the same trigger styling (`sm:opacity-0 sm:group-hover:opacity-100
sm:group-focus-within:opacity-100`, so it's hover-revealed on desktop and always visible below
the `sm` breakpoint, unchanged). `getRowActions`, `ACTION_SUCCESS`, `ACTION_DIALOG` and the
confirm-dialog flow were untouched. The table wrapper's `overflow-x: auto` was left exactly as
it was, per the stage's instruction.

Searched `src/` for other dropdowns/popovers rendered inside an overflow container, per the
stage's "Other usages" instruction. Found none: `Chat.jsx` and `SupplierDetail.jsx` only use
`overflow-y-auto`/`overflow-hidden` for scrollable lists or rounded card clipping, with no
absolutely-positioned menu inside them; `AdminSuppliers.jsx` (the stage's own "e.g." example)
has no dropdown/popover at all — its only `absolute` elements are a modal backdrop and a search
icon. Nothing to migrate, so nothing to ask about.

Wrote `frontend/tests/components/ActionMenu.test.jsx` (11 tests, mocking
`HTMLElement.prototype.getBoundingClientRect` and `window.innerHeight`): portal rendering (menu
is in `document.body`, not under the trigger's own container), opens-below vs. flips-above
positioning math, the 8px left clamp, and every close path (outside mousedown, Escape with
focus return, item selection calling the handler exactly once, `resize`, a `scroll` event
dispatched on a nested element to exercise the capture-phase listener, and only one menu open at
a time across two sibling `ActionMenu` instances — the last one needed an explicit
`fireEvent.mouseDown` before the second trigger's click, since `fireEvent.click` alone doesn't
synthesize the `mousedown` a real click produces, which is what closes the first menu). Also a
renders-nothing-with-no-items case.

## 2026-11-04 — Credit Service: administrator transaction filters by user and order

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-opus-5)
**Mode:** generate
**Scope:** Implementation code
**Governing decision:** The user's instruction of 2026-11-04, quoted below. The endpoint surface itself has no FR behind it — recorded as a gap in `credit-service/credit-service-context.md` §10 item 10 rather than treated as a requirement.

**Prompts (exact):**

> Add two admin query filters to credit-service. Read CONTEXT.md and API.md first.
>
> ## What to build
>
> Extend the existing `GET /credits/transactions/all` with two optional query parameters:
>
> ?userId=<uuid> rows where that user is the originating OR the destination user
> ?requestId=<uuid> rows for that order
>
> Both optional, both combinable (AND them). No parameters means the current behaviour, unchanged.
>
> Do NOT add a new route. This is a filter on the existing admin endpoint so it inherits the auth gate, the pagination and the row shape rather than duplicating them.
>
> ## Rules
>
> - Auth unchanged: bearer token, rank >= admin, so super admin is included. Mirror the existing roleRank comparison.
> - Response shape unchanged. Same fields, same keyset pagination, 20 per page, newest first. No new fields.
> - An unknown or unmatched filter returns 200 with an empty array, NOT 404. Credit-service has no view of which orders or users exist, and an order with no transactions yet is a normal state.
> - A malformed UUID returns 400 with the existing INVALID_REQUEST_BODY code. Validate with the same zod approach used elsewhere.
> - Cursor pagination must still work with a filter applied — the cursor has to carry the filter or the filter must be re-applied on the next page. Say which you did.
>
> ## Report, don't decide
>
> `transaction_log` has indexes on originating_user_id and destination_user_id, both `(user, created_at DESC)`. For request_id there are only the three partial unique indexes, each covering one transaction type, so a plain `WHERE request_id = $1` may not use them well.
>
> Report whether a general index on request_id is warranted, and what adding one would cost — init.sql only runs on an empty volume, so it would mean another `docker compose down -v`. Do not add it without asking.
>
> ## Also
>
> - Update API.md with both parameters, the combined case, the empty result behaviour and the error codes.
> - Record in CONTEXT.md §10 that this endpoint surface has no FR behind it. F19.5.2 covers own-transactions and F20.2 covers all-transactions; an admin filter by user or order is new. It is driven by user-service's F5.3.2. Note it as a gap, do not invent a requirement.
>
> ## Tests
>
> - filter by userId returns only rows where they are originating or destination, and nothing else
> - filter by requestId returns only that order's rows
> - both together
> - no filter still returns everything, as before
> - a non-admin is still 403 with a filter applied
> - an unmatched filter is 200 with an empty array
> - a malformed UUID is 400
> - pagination still works correctly with a filter across two pages
>
> Mutation-check it: break the filter so it is ignored, and confirm a test fails. If nothing fails, the tests aren't testing the filter.
>
> ## Afterwards
>
> Report what changed, what you verified, and anything you had to invent. Nothing outside credit-service/ should need touching — flag it if that turns out to be wrong.

**Key responses:**

_One code path, two intents._ `listTransactions` now takes a `TransactionFilters` object rather than a bare `userId`. The administrator's `userId` filter is the same SQL predicate F19.5.2 already uses to scope a caller to their own rows — originating OR destination — so both go through one path instead of two that could drift. The service layer keeps the intent distinct with a comment: for F19.5.2 the id comes from the verified token and is not the caller's to choose, which is why that route still has no user parameter.

_Cursor._ Filters travel **beside** the cursor, not inside it. The cursor stays an opaque position token (`created_at|transaction_id`) and the caller re-sends `?userId=…&cursor=…`. The trade-off is that dropping the filter on a later page silently widens the result instead of erroring; a test pins that documented behaviour rather than leaving it assumed. Encoding filters into the cursor would have made the mismatch impossible, at the cost of a cursor that is no longer a pure position and cannot be reused across queries.

_Validation._ Both parameters are zod `z.string().uuid().optional()`, parsed through the existing `parseBody` helper, so a malformed value is `400 INVALID_REQUEST_BODY` before any query runs rather than a Postgres cast error surfacing as a 500.

**Verification actually run:**

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Full suite **142 tests in 14 files, all passing** (123 in 13 before).
- The new `tests/http/transactionFilters.test.ts` is 19 tests covering every case the brief listed, plus a user who is only ever a destination, a user who exists with no credit activity, and the dropped-filter-on-page-two behaviour.
- **Mutation checks, two, both caught.** Making the `requestId` filter a no-op fails 6 tests; making the `userId` filter a no-op fails 4. The second also breaks `tests/http/transactions.test.ts > does not leak another user's rows`, because the administrator filter and the F19.5.2 scope share a code path — so the mutation that would silently widen an admin query is the same one that would leak a user's history.
- **Index measurement** (see Deviations): built a 200 000-row scratch database from the real `init.sql`, compared plans, dropped it afterwards. The dev database holds 11 rows, far too few for Postgres to choose anything but a sequential scan.

**Files:**

- `credit-service/src/db/queries/credits.queries.ts` (modified: `TransactionFilters`)
- `credit-service/src/services/credits.service.ts` (modified)
- `credit-service/src/controllers/credits.controller.ts` (modified)
- `credit-service/tests/http/transactionFilters.test.ts` (created)
- `credit-service/API.md` (modified: filters, combined case, empty-result behaviour, error codes, invented-items list)
- `credit-service/credit-service-context.md` (modified: §10 item 10)
- `ai/usage-log.md` (modified)
- `README.md` (modified: Log index row)

**Deviations / questions raised for the team:**

1. **A general index on `request_id` is measured but NOT added**, pending the team's decision. On 200 000 rows: without one, a `WHERE request_id = $1` is a Parallel Seq Scan, 2 318 shared buffers, **8.855 ms**; with `transaction_log (request_id)` it is an Index Scan, 10 buffers, **0.100 ms** — about 88× faster. The three existing partial unique indexes cannot serve it because each is `WHERE transaction_type = '…'` and this query does not filter on type. Cost: **6.2 MB per 200 000 rows** (~12% on top of a 50 MB relation), one more B-tree insert on every credit write — which is the same transaction NFR8.2.1's unmeasured 500 ms budget covers — and a `docker compose down -v` on credit-db, because `init.sql` only runs on an empty volume. My read, which is not a decision: not warranted at current scale, and cheapest folded into whichever change next forces a volume teardown.
2. **The brief's attribution of this surface to user-service's F5.3.2 is only half right.** F5.3.2 exists and reads _"The system shall allow administrators to view transaction details of individual users"_ (`docs/FoC-ProductBacklog.md` line 103), which backs the `userId` filter. It does **not** cover `?requestId=`; filtering by order has no requirement in this backlog or user-service's and was requested directly. §10 item 10 records the two halves separately rather than letting F5.3.2 appear to justify the whole surface.
3. **Invented, and listed in `API.md` under "What was invented" as item 4a:** the parameter names `userId` and `requestId`; that unknown query keys are ignored rather than rejected, matching the existing cursor handling; that an unmatched filter is an empty `200`; and that filters travel beside the cursor rather than inside it.
4. **Nothing outside `credit-service/` needed touching**, as the brief expected — apart from this log entry and its README row, which AGENTS.md §5 and §6 require.

**Key responses:**

_Arrangement._ Not really a choice: `compose.dev.yaml` already declared a `frontend` service on `target: dev` with Compose Watch, and the base simply never had one. Adding the base service on `target: prod` completes the pattern order-service already follows, so `docker compose up` yields a working system and the dev overlay keeps hot reload.

_No build-time configuration._ Confirmed by search: nothing under `frontend/src` or `index.html` reads `import.meta.env`, every call is a same-origin relative path, and the Socket.IO client connects with no URL. So the single-origin-through-nginx approach needs nothing baked into the bundle.

_Request-time DNS._ Upstreams go through a variable plus `resolver 127.0.0.11`. With a literal `proxy_pass`, nginx resolves every upstream while loading its config and refuses to start if one is missing — which would mean the frontend could not serve a static asset until all four backends were up. `$request_uri` is explicit because nginx stops appending the URI once `proxy_pass` contains a variable.

**Verification actually run:**

All five checks confirmed, after recreating the `user-db` and `credit-db` volumes together (synthetic data, at the user's instruction; credit balances are keyed to user UUIDs, so recreating one without the other would orphan rows).

2. **Full `docker compose up`** — all 14 services. The frontend could not bind 5173 because the user's own host Vite server holds it, so it was brought up on `FRONTEND_PORT=8099` rather than killing their server; on a clean machine 5173 is free.
3. **End to end in a browser, through nginx** — registered a fresh user, activated by OTP, and **the credit-allocation outbox fired for the first time ever on this stack**: outbox row `sent` with 0 attempts, and a `balances` row of 20 credits. Then in Chromium against `:8099`: login through `/auth/login`, Wallet showing `20 available · 0 reserved · 20 total`, nav pill `20 cr`, history paging 20 rows then 25 after scroll, zero page errors. Paths exercised through nginx: `/assets/*`, `/auth/login`, `/auth/refresh`, `/users/me`, `/credits/balance`, `/credits/transactions`, `/wallet`.
4. **Deep route** — `GET /wallet` returns 200 `text/html`; the SPA then guards it to `/login` and returns to `/wallet` after signing in.
5. **Host `npm run dev`** — still 200 on 5173 throughout, and the merged dev config publishes exactly one port.

Every proxy path was additionally confirmed to reach a _distinct_ backend by its error envelope: credit-service's `{"error":{"code":…}}`, supplier-service's `{"status_code":…}`, user-service's `{"message":…}`, and Engine.IO's own `{"code":0,"message":"Transport unknown"}` on `/socket.io`.

**Files:**

- `frontend/Dockerfile` (modified: `build` and `prod` stages)
- `frontend/nginx/default.conf`, `frontend/nginx/proxy-headers.inc` (created)
- `compose.yaml` (modified: `frontend` service)
- `compose.dev.yaml` (modified: `ports: !override`)
- `order-service/Dockerfile` (modified: see Deviations 1)
- `README.md` (modified: running the stack, the volume warning, the TLS gap, Log index row)

**Deviations / questions raised for the team:**

1. **The postinstall hook committed in `6f3c174` had broken `docker build` for order-service, and main has been broken since that merged.** The deps stage copies only `package.json` and the lockfile before `npm ci`, so npm tried to run `scripts/prisma-generate.mjs` before that file existed. The script's existing guard covered a missing _schema_, not a missing _script_. Nobody had noticed because the running containers predate the change and nothing had rebuilt since; it surfaced on the first `docker compose up --build` after it. Fixed by copying `scripts/` before `npm ci`, in a separate commit, and verified with `docker build --target production`. **This was my own regression from the CI task, missed because I verified `npm ci` on the host but never re-ran the Docker build after adding the hook.**
2. **`ports: !override` requires Docker Compose 2.24.4.** Established by running the real binaries, since the documentation does not state it: on 2.24.3 the tag is _silently ignored_ and the port lists concatenate, so the first `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.dev.yaml up` fails with "port is already allocated" — for other people and not for the author. The team is checking `docker compose version`. A version-proof alternative exists (give prod a different host port and drop the tag) and was offered.
3. **The first healthcheck reported unhealthy for 18 minutes.** Inside the container `localhost` resolves to `::1` only, and nginx's `listen 80` binds IPv4, so `wget http://localhost/healthz` was refused while the port worked from outside. Fixed by probing `127.0.0.1` and adding `listen [::]:80`, which is right for a production edge anyway.
4. **No TLS.** nginx listens on plain HTTP. With Option A this file becomes the production edge, so tokens, refresh cookies and passwords would cross the network in clear text. Recorded in the README and at the top of the nginx config; unowned.
5. **Invented, none of it a team decision:** `nginx:1.27-alpine` and its pin; `/healthz` as the probe path and `wget --spider` as the command; the caching policy (immutable for `/assets/`, `no-cache` for `index.html`); request-time resolution over literal upstreams; the 3600s WebSocket timeout; `frontend/nginx/` as the config directory.
6. **Log index row 155 is also claimed by the credit-service admin-filters branch**, which is pushed but not merged. Whoever merges second renumbers, as with the two previous collisions.
7. **`user-service/.env` needed four Stage 18 variables** (`LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES` and friends) before it would boot. Local and gitignored, not committed — but it is the same recurring problem: user-service is the only service whose configuration lives in a gitignored file, so every new required variable breaks it silently for everyone who already has one.

**Key responses:**

_Fix 1._ One `docker-build` matrix job, five legs, `fail-fast: false` so a single broken image does not hide the state of the other four. Only the deploy target is built; `base`, `deps` and `build` are its ancestors, so a break anywhere in that chain fails the leg. Caching is `type=gha` through `setup-buildx-action` — the default docker driver cannot export cache — scoped per `service-target` so the five legs do not evict one another from the 10 GB per-repository cache. Same triggers and no `needs`, so each leg appears as its own PR check exactly as the five test jobs do.

_The target-name divergence is spelled out, not normalised._ `order-service` is `production`; the other four are `prod`. Recorded as a matrix value with a comment pointing at the PR note rather than renamed, because renaming that stage would also mean editing `compose.yaml` and `compose.dev.yaml`, which belongs to order-service's owner.

_Fix 2, gate check._ AGENTS.md does **not** mandate the numbering. Its §6 template is four columns — `Date | Service | Entry | High-level summary` — with no `#` column, so removing it moves the README _towards_ the documented format rather than away from it. No AGENTS.md change was needed and none was made.

_Fix 2 turned up an unrelated defect._ The README held **two** Log index tables, not one: lines 175–304 (128 rows) and 305–461 (155 rows). Almost certainly the 2026-11-03 merge-conflict resolution recorded in the entry above, which kept both sides' rows and in fact kept both sides' whole tables. Rows 1–126 were duplicates, but the stale table's last two rows existed **nowhere else** — `Order service: 404 for missing or non-UUID order ids` and `Frontend: required-field asterisks on the create-errand form`, both of which are real entries in this log (2026-10-22). Deleting the stale table outright would have silently dropped two disclosures. They were reinstated in the position `ai/usage-log.md` itself gives them, and the result is one table of 157 rows.

**Mode:** generate
**Scope:** Implementation code
**Governing decision:** `instructions.md`, "Stage 23: Session Lifetime and Expiry Warning (NFR4)" and "Stage 23c: Expiry Warning Banner — Frontend".

**Prompts (exact):**

> let's branch off for 23c

> okay, let's continue with 23c then

**Key responses:**
Read the current code against the Stage 23c table first: `AuthContext.jsx` already held `user`/`status`/`login`/`logout`/`forceReauth`; `http.js` already had the single-callback `setOnSessionExpired` pattern (used for the existing session-expiry redirect) and `refreshAccessToken()`, which every one of the stage's four read points except login funnels through (session restore, the proactive refresh, and the refresh-after-401 retry in `send()` all call it); `auth.js`'s `login()` makes its own `POST /auth/login` call instead. No disagreement with the stage text, so implemented directly, choosing (and reporting, per the stage's "put the text in your summary" instruction) how to wire the four read points and where the lead-time constant and banner component live.

Added `setOnSessionTimeLeft`/`recordSessionTimeLeft` to `http.js`, mirroring the existing `setOnSessionExpired` single-callback pattern: `refreshAccessToken()` now also calls it with the response's `sessionTimeLeftSeconds` (covers session restore, proactive refresh, refresh-after-401 in one place), and `auth.js`'s `login()` calls `recordSessionTimeLeft` directly with its own response's value (the one read point that bypasses `refreshAccessToken`).

In `AuthContext.jsx`: added `LEAD_TIME_MS` (the named 10-minute constant the stage asked for) and `sessionDeadline` (a `performance.now()`-based monotonic timestamp, set from the new callback) plus `sessionExpiringSoon`, exposed on the context. `sessionExpiringSoon` is recomputed by an effect keyed on `[isLoggedIn, sessionDeadline]` rather than polled. That effect originally scheduled one `setTimeout` for the remaining delay; testing caught that a fresh 30-day deadline's delay (~2.59×10⁹ ms) overflows `setTimeout`'s 32-bit signed delay ceiling (~2.147×10⁹ ms) and fires almost immediately instead of ~30 days later, which would have shown the banner right after every login. Fixed by chunking the wait into steps of at most `MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` and rescheduling until the real deadline is reached — this was not something I flagged as a design question since it is purely a `setTimeout` platform limit, not a product decision. The deadline is cleared (set to `null`) in `logout()`, `forceReauth()`, and the `onSessionExpired` handler, so it never carries over to the next login, per the stage's "On logout" bullet.

Created `SessionExpiryBanner.jsx`: visually reuses `FormBanner`'s `info` tone classes (`border-line`/`bg-surface-alt`/`text-ink-70`) rather than rendering `FormBanner` itself, since `FormBanner` only accepts a message string and this banner needs a non-dismissible "Log in again" button (calling `AuthContext.logout()`, same as `TopNav`'s existing control) and spans the full page width rather than sitting inside a form — reported here per the stage's instruction to put the choice in the summary for review. Mounted it in `App.jsx` directly above `TopNav`, outside the `<Routes>`, so it shows at the top of every page regardless of route.

**Banner text (for review):** "Your session will end soon. Log in again to keep working." — does not promise an exact sign-out time, per the stage's requirement.

Could not visually verify the banner in an actual browser — no browser tool was available in this session (built-in browser cannot reach a container-local `localhost`; Claude in Chrome was not connected) — so the UI was not eyeballed end-to-end; the author should click through it manually (`docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.dev.yaml up -d user-db user-service frontend` is already running).

Tests added in `frontend/tests/context/AuthContext.test.jsx`, mocking the network layer (`fetch`) directly rather than the `api/*` modules, per the stage's "mock the network layer" instruction, with a fresh module registry (`vi.resetModules`) per test so `http.js`'s module-level state can't leak between tests: no banner after a 30-day restore; a 15-minute restore shows no banner, then one after 5 fake-timer minutes pass; a 5-minute restore shows the banner immediately; the banner has no dismiss control; "Log in again" logs out and the banner disappears; the deadline does not carry over to a fresh login after logout (the test that caught the `setTimeout` overflow above); a refresh-after-401 response also updates the deadline. **Mode:** docs
**Scope:** Requirements formatting | Refactor/Docs
**Governing decision:** The team's chat answers of 2026-11-05 (quoted below); recorded as B1–B16 in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-supplier-bookmarking-design.md`.

**Prompts (exact):**

> In my supplier service, I want to add a functionality for users to bookmark their favorite locations. The idea is that these can appear at the top of the supplier page before the user searches for anything in particular. This will be in a new supplier-bookmarking branch.
> Ask the necessary decision questions, if any, to design this feature with me. I see it as a very small change, likely just storing each user's bookmarked suppliers somewhere in the supplier service, so that when a specific user queries for the inital home page load, these bookmarked suppliers will be sent to facilitate the pinned display

> 1. in this change, i meant the bookmarked supplier cards. locations will be another change.
> 2. the more robust solution is for the returned suppliers to already contain a isBookmarked flag that is computed in the backend from a comparison with a list of user-level bookmarked suppliers. This would allow the flag to be shown whenever that supplier appears on screen
> 3. all can bookmark, but bookmarking is user-specific. One will not bookmark for everyone. this means that we are not storing an additional universal field for suppliers. Hence I said that we will need a separate table to store the favourites. I am inclined to put this into user-service, which should already be maintaining user-specific details.
> 4. user-service stores the bookmarkings in an appropriate table in user-service, or even a new table in user-service. Typically, the bookmarking can be rendered on the user side with a simple comparison of the ids and their personal list. But the user can also filter by saved, of which theoir list of bookmarked supplier ids will be sent to the supplier service so the supplier service can return the marked suppliers separately
> 5. since the supplier-service returns the results, hidden or deleted suppliers will just not show up
> 6. lets set maximum to be 20 bookmarks per user. Clicking on the bookmark icon bookmarks it, the icon will change state, and clicking again will unbookmark the supplier. By default, ordering will follow the same per location sectioning the supplier page already applies
> 7. Since Adding and removing bookmarks uses the same button, is this an issue?
> 8. start from main
> 9. this will touch user-service, the fe under user-service, and a little of supplier-service

> 1. Agree with the button firing different endpoints based on the current state of the icon
> 2. lets ditch theisBookmarked flag. As menioned in 4, the user side will render the bookmarking by comparing with their own list. If the user requests to filter just by bookmarked, the ids will be sent. This keeps cross service communication more contained
> 3. When the user filters by bookmarked and the supplier-service sees that any of the bookmarks point to a hidden or deleted supplier, the supplier-service will return "hidden" and "deleted" respectively. If the entry is "deleted", the user service side will remove that bookmark. If it is hidden, the bookmark will be retained.

> 1. Yes, follow existing route conventions. 422 can be used for 21st bookmark with accompanying user-oriented message along the lines of "You can only bookmark 20 locations! Unbookmark another before bookmarking this" (tighten up the language for the actual)
> 2. Yes new table. Adding a supplier that doesnt exist will be gated on the fe with the icon. Even if the user somehow gets around that, that id will be sent during a filter for "saved" call. Thats when the supplier service can perform the check - following the response suggestion from 3, such a supplier that does not exist will return the same status of "deleted" and cleared from the user table.
> 3. yes, the IDs can be passed in the existing endpoint. What do you mean by where do hidden and deleted status go? They are part of the return payload, and would be ignored by the fe entirely so nothing will be displayed, as there is no information anyway. Filters can still be applied on top of the saved suppliers
> 4. yes, the fe calls user-service's bookmark delete (unbookmark) endpoint
> 5. ditch the pin. the filter works just fine
> 6. yes. hidden counts towards the cap as they can be reenabled, but deleted will be cleared on the next saved filter load

> 1. yes, filter parameter just uses the existing list endpoint.
> 2. extra array works
> 3. hidden ids will be under the unavailable array and ignored from filters, as you suggested
> 4. yes.
> 5. yes
>    proceed with spec and plan

**Key responses:**

- Asked the decision questions instead of choosing (this is architecture/design work under root `AGENTS.md` §2.1): which entity is bookmarked, where the data lives, the response shape, the cap, hidden/deleted handling and the base branch. Recorded the team's answers as B1–B16.
- Created the local branch `supplier-bookmarking` from `main` (no files changed by that step).
- Wrote the spec and a 3-part, TDD-style implementation plan (user-service, supplier-service, frontend) from those decisions only. Where the team had not decided something, the spec's "Not yet decided by the team" table (G1–G7) shows the plan's working choice: soft-deleted wins over inactive, `code` string names, `400` for a bad id, `422` for an empty `ids=`, placement of the Saved filter in the UI, a composite primary key, and oldest-first ordering of the id list.
- Noted that the user-service mounts these routes at `/users/me/*`, so the new routes are `/users/me/bookmarks`, not the `/me/bookmarks` written in an earlier question.
- Added workstream W8 (Planned) to `supplier-service/PROJECT_STATE.md`.
- Verification: none run. No code was written or executed; the plan's code was written against files read in this session and has not been compiled or tested.

## 2026-11-05 — Supplier bookmarking: spec and plan updated for the team's gap answers

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-sonnet-5-5)
**Mode:** docs
**Scope:** Requirements formatting | Refactor/Docs
**Governing decision:** The team's chat answers below; recorded as B17–B22 in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-supplier-bookmarking-design.md`.

**Prompts (exact):**

> 1. delete take precedence. Use deleted if both are active
> 2. Codename works
> 3. bad supplier ids will not exist in a typical flow - only via injections. The supplier service will return a dedicated status "invalid" that follows the same logic as "deleted" and be removed. Other valid ids are not blocked
> 4. if there are no saved suppliers, filtering by bookmark should just return an empty payload which the fe can render as "No bookmarked supplier"
> 5. Use "Bookmarked" as the label in place of Saved
> 6. Table keys are correct
> 7. oldest id first works - whatever the supplier replies

**Key responses:**

- Recorded the answers in the spec (B17–B22) and cut the open-gaps table to what is still undecided (G3, G5, G8–G10).
- Updated the plan: a malformed item in `ids` no longer fails the request (the parameter now parses to `{ valid, invalid }`); the service returns an `invalid` entry for each and an empty payload when nothing is well-formed or `ids` is empty; the frontend clears `deleted` and `invalid` entries; the filter is labelled "Bookmarked".
- Found that the frontend's request helper (`frontend/src/api/http.js`) drops empty query values, so an empty `ids` would never reach the service and the call would list every supplier. The plan therefore keeps a frontend shortcut that shows the empty state itself when there are no bookmarks, alongside the service behaviour the team asked for.
- Wording choices not given by the team: the empty-state text "No bookmarked suppliers." (you wrote "No bookmarked supplier") and the order of `unavailable` entries (well-formed first, then malformed).
- Verification: none run. Documents only; no code was written or executed.

## 2026-11-05 — Stage 24: Admin User History Page (F5.3.2)

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-sonnet-5)
**Mode:** generate
**Scope:** Implementation code
**Governing decision:** `instructions.md` Stage 24 (frontend-only; backend contracts already merged on main).

**Prompts (exact):**

> can we implement stage 24? let me know if you have anything that you're unsure about first.

> (AskUserQuestion) What should the order page show when the supplier name can't be resolved (supplier-service down or id not found)? → "Supplier \<id\>"

**Key responses:**

- Found one unresolved `[DECIDE]` placeholder in Stage 24 (fallback text for a missing supplier name); the stage's own rule says to stop and ask rather than pick a value, so asked the team before writing any code. Recorded the answer ("Supplier \<id\>", matching the existing "Location \<id\>" pattern) directly into `instructions.md`.
- Added `getUser` (user-service `GET /users/:id`), `getOrder` and `listUserOrders` (order-service `GET /orders/:id`, `GET /orders/admin/users/:userId`), and `listOrderTransactions` (credit-service `GET /credits/transactions/all?requestId=`) to the existing `api/*.js` modules, following their established style (JSDoc-style contract comments, thin `request()` wrappers).
- Found and reported a mismatch while checking each service's error shape (Stage 24a's own instruction): `http.js`'s `ApiError` only read `body.message`/`body.code`, which works for user/order-service but leaves both `undefined` for credit-service's documented `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope. Fixed by having `ApiError` fall back to the nested `error.message`/`error.code` only when the top-level ones are absent, which does not change order-service's own `body.error` (a string there, not an object) or any other existing caller.
- Built `AdminUserTransactions.jsx` (route `/admin/user-transactions/:userId`) and `AdminOrderTransactions.jsx` (route `/admin/user-transactions/:userId/:requestId`), per the stage's design-decision table: profile + suspend/unsuspend/promote/demote (reusing `AdminUsers.jsx`'s exact `getRowActions`/`ACTION_SUCCESS`/`ACTION_DIALOG`/`ConfirmActionDialog`, now exported from there instead of duplicated, so the two pages can't drift from each other's allowed-actions table); a paginated, client-side-filterable (role/status) order list with the page number kept in the URL; the order page's full field list and its transactions, with credits colour/sign reusing `credits.js`'s `describe()` (held/returned, no sign, for reservation/release; signed for transfer) relative to the viewed user. A profile 404, or an order that is missing or doesn't involve the viewed user, takes over the whole page ("not found"); the orders section and the transactions section each fail and retry independently of everything else, per the stage's "Section failures" rule.
- Wired the entry point: `/admin/users` rows now navigate to the new user page on click; the three-dot menu's cell and the email eye-icon button stop the click from bubbling so they still work without navigating. Added the two routes to `App.jsx` behind `RequireAuth` + `RequireRole(minimum="admin")`.
- Verification run: `npm run lint` (oxlint) clean of errors (same pre-existing warning patterns as the rest of the codebase, e.g. `set-state-in-effect`); `npm run build` (vite) succeeds; `npx vitest run` — 19 files / 97 tests pass, including the two new test files and the extended `AdminUsers.test.jsx` (which needed a `MemoryRouter` wrapper added to its `renderPage()`, since `AdminUsers.jsx` now calls `useNavigate` unconditionally). Did not open a browser; no backend services were running, so this is lint/build/unit-test verification only, not the manual browser checklist.

## 2026-11-06 — Stage 25a/25c: Backend — Retry-After on OTP_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED and counting guesses against an expired code

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-sonnet-5)
**Mode:** generate
**Scope:** Implementation code
**Governing decision:** `instructions.md` Stage 25 ("Stage 25: OTP \"Attempts Exceeded\" Dead-End Fix (backend + frontend)", including the "Design decisions (already made, do not change)" table, and sub-stages 25a and 25c).

**Prompts (exact):**

> let's implement stage 25. remember the git workflow

**Key responses:**

- Read `otp.service.ts`, `otp.queries.ts`, `app.ts`'s error handler, and every `checkOtp` call site (`auth.service.ts`: `verifyRegistrationOtp`, `verifyForgotPasswordOtp` (consume=false), `resetPassword`; `me.service.ts`: `verifyEmailChangeOtp`, `confirmPasswordChange`) before changing anything, per the file's instruction to read the current code first.
- Confirmed the global error handler in `app.ts` already checks `err.retryAfterSeconds !== undefined` (not truthiness), so 25a needed no change there.
- All 5 `checkOtp` call sites handled a failure identically (`if (!result.ok) throw new AppError(400, 'Invalid or expired OTP', 'INVALID_OTP')`, after the transaction commits), so none needed special-case handling; added a shared `throwOtpFailure` helper in `otp.service.ts` and switched all 5 to call it instead.
- `checkOtp` in `otp.service.ts`: reordered checks to missing/consumed (throw INVALID_OTP, unchanged) → attempts exhausted (throw 429 OTP_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED directly, with `Retry-After` from a new `otpRetryAfterSeconds(row)` helper computed from `row.created_at`/`row.db_now`, both already fetched by `findLatestOtp` on the same DB clock) → expired (now increments attempts and **returns** `{ ok: false, reason: 'expired', ... }` instead of throwing, so the increment survives the commit) → hash mismatch (increments and returns `{ ok: false, reason: 'invalid', ... }`) → hash match (consume as before). Added a `CheckOtpResult` type and a `failedAttempt` helper shared by the expired and wrong-guess paths; both call `incrementAttempts`, and if the new count has reached `max_attempts`, set `exhausted: true` and the same `otpRetryAfterSeconds` value, so `throwOtpFailure` throws 429 `OTP_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED` with `Retry-After` for the 5th failure instead of `INVALID_OTP`/`OTP_EXPIRED`.
- `otp.queries.ts`: `incrementAttempts` now does `attempts_count = LEAST(attempts_count + 1, max_attempts)` so a guess against an already-exhausted, still-expired code (which reaches `failedAttempt` only if the attempts check above it somehow didn't fire first — not reachable in the new order, but kept as a safety cap per the file's explicit instruction) cannot push the `SMALLINT` column past `max_attempts`.
- Updated existing tests that depended on the old order/shape: `tests/services/otp.service.test.ts` (`checkOtp` describe block — the old "OTP_EXPIRED always throws" and "429 at max_attempts" tests, plus every `{ ok: false }` assertion, which now carries a `reason`), `tests/db/queries/otp.queries.test.ts` (added a cap test for `incrementAttempts`), `tests/controllers/auth.controller.test.ts` (registration verify-otp, forgot-password verify-otp, reset-password — each "5 wrong OTPs, then correct" test rewritten as "4 wrong → 400 each; 5th wrong → 429 with Retry-After; correct afterwards → still 429"), `tests/controllers/me.controller.test.ts` (verify-otp for change-email, confirm-password-change — same rewrite). Added new test cases for: expired-code attempts counting, the check-order (expired-and-exhausted → 429 with `Retry-After: 0`), and mixed wrong/expired guesses sharing one `attempts_count`.
- Verification run: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx eslint` on every changed file clean; `npx vitest run` — full suite, 31 files / 852 tests pass (against the real Postgres test DB on the running `foc-user-db` container).

## 2026-11-06 — Stage 25b: Frontend — OTP attempts-exceeded UI fix

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-sonnet-5)
**Mode:** generate
**Scope:** Implementation code
**Governing decision:** `instructions.md` Stage 25's "Design decisions (already made, do not change)" table and the "Stage 25b: Frontend" section.

**Prompts (exact):**

> let's implement stage 25. remember the git workflow
> go ahead
> go for it

**Key responses:**

- Read `frontend/` first per the stage's instruction, and reported how `Retry-After` reaches `ResendButton` before changing anything: `api/http.js`'s `send()` already parses the `Retry-After` header into `ApiError.retryAfterSeconds` (`undefined` if missing) for every non-ok response, not only the resend endpoint, so `OTP_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED` already carried it; the gap was that nothing outside `ResendButton`'s own `onResend` catch could start its countdown, and `OtpInput`'s existing `disabled` prop already supported a "dead" state (no new prop needed).
- `http.js`: no change, per the stage's "if it already does, change nothing."
- `OtpInput.jsx`: no change; reused the existing `disabled` prop.
- `ResendButton.jsx`: converted to `forwardRef` and added an imperative `startCooldown(seconds)` handle (same pattern as `OtpInput`'s `reset()`), plus a new `initialCooldown` prop that seeds the same state on mount. Existing `OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN`/`OTP_RESEND_LIMIT` handling in `handleClick` is unchanged.
- `errorMessages.js`: reworded `OTP_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED`. Old: "Too many incorrect attempts. Request a new code." New: "That code is no longer valid. You can request a new one once the button below is available."
- `Register.jsx`, `Account.jsx` (`EmailSection`, `PasswordSection`): on `OTP_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED`, clear the boxes, disable them (new `otpDead` state), show the reworded message, and start the resend countdown via `resendRef.current.startCooldown(err.retryAfterSeconds ?? 0)`. On `OTP_EXPIRED`, clear/refocus but keep enabled (previously these two codes shared one branch with a " Use resend below." suffix; split them since Stage 25 gives them different box behaviour). A successful resend re-enables and clears the boxes and the error.
- `ForgotPassword.jsx`: same for the step-2 `onOtpComplete`, extracted into a shared `applyOtpBoxEffect` helper. **Found and fixed a real bug while writing the step-3 fallback test**: when `resetPassword` (step 3) itself returns `OTP_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED` (the 5th failed attempt) and the page falls back from step 3 to step 2, step 2's `ResendButton` is not mounted yet at the moment the error arrives (step 3 has no OTP step), so `resendRef.current` is `null` and `startCooldown` would be a no-op — the countdown would silently fail to start. Fixed by adding a `resendCooldown` state passed as `ResendButton`'s new `initialCooldown` prop, so the countdown is correct the instant it (re)mounts in step 2, in addition to the `startCooldown` ref call used by the already-mounted case (`onOtpComplete`).
- Registration arrived-from-login flow: re-checked against the actual code (`Login.jsx` only ever redirects to `/register` with `{ step: 'otp' }` on `ACCOUNT_NOT_VERIFIED`, never carrying an `OTP_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED` condition) and found no distinct "entered with `OTP_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED`" code path for this flow to wire up beyond the normal `onOtpComplete` handler, which already covers it uniformly since `arrivedFromLogin` only toggles which single `ResendButton` instance renders (the two are mutually exclusive), not the failure-handling logic itself.
- **Observation, not fixed (out of scope / pre-existing, not introduced by this stage):** found via a test's focus assertion that `OtpInput`'s `reset()` call inside `onOtpComplete`'s catch block cannot actually move focus to the first box, because `otpBusy` (and therefore `OtpInput`'s `disabled` prop) is still `true` in the DOM at that point — React batches the `setOtpBusy(false)` in the `finally` block together with the catch's state updates, so the live DOM element is still disabled when `.focus()` is called, and a disabled input can't receive focus. This already affects the pre-existing `INVALID_OTP` path on all four pages (not something Stage 25 touches), so it was left alone and only asserted on value-clearing, not focus, in the new tests.
- Added new test files (none existed for these components/pages before this stage): `tests/components/OtpInput.test.jsx`, `tests/components/ResendButton.test.jsx` (fake timers for the countdown, including the new `startCooldown`/`initialCooldown`), `tests/pages/Register.test.jsx`, `tests/pages/ForgotPassword.test.jsx` (including the step-3 fallback), `tests/pages/Account.test.jsx` (`EmailSection` and `PasswordSection`).
- Verification run: `npx oxlint .` clean of errors/warnings on every changed file (pre-existing warnings elsewhere in the codebase are unrelated); `npm run build` (vite) succeeds; `npx vitest run` — 24 files / 124 tests pass. Did not start the dev server or open a browser; no backend services were rebuilt with the Stage 25a/25c changes in their running container, so this is lint/build/unit-test verification only, not the manual browser Verification checklist.

Two `LEFT JOIN users` (aliased `actor_user`/`target_user`) resolve both usernames; a deleted user leaves that alias's columns NULL. `reasonCode=OTHER` matches `reason LIKE 'OTHER: %'`; any other code is an exact `reason = $code` match.
- `src/constants/auditReasons.ts`: added `AUDIT_ACTIONS` (the six valid values, for the `action` filter) and `ALL_REASON_CODES` (the deduplicated union of every action's preset codes, for the `reasonCode` filter, which isn't tied to one action).
- `auditLog.service.ts` (new): `listAuditLogs(params)`, `PAGE_SIZE = 50`, maps the query's snake_case/joined-alias row to the camelCase `AuditLogEntry` shape from the decisions table.
- `auditLog.controller.ts` (new): Zod `.strict()` on `req.query`. `page` reuses Stage 15b's single-message pattern; `actor`/`target` lowercase+trim and treat a repeated param (which Express turns into an array) as the field's own "must be a string" case, satisfying "a repeated param on a single-value filter -> 400" without a separate message; `action` accepts one value or several (repeatable param) against `AUDIT_ACTIONS`; `reasonCode` against `ALL_REASON_CODES`; `from`/`to` parse via `new Date(value)`, invalid -> the exact messages the doc gives; a `superRefine` on the whole object rejects `from` after `to`. `sortDir` only (`asc`/`desc`, default `desc`); no `sortBy` field is declared, so one is rejected by `.strict()`'s own "unexpected field" path, per the doc's "`sortBy=anything` -> 400 (unexpected field)" bullet - no special-casing needed.
- `auditLog.routes.ts` (new) + mounted at `/admin/audit-logs` in `app.ts`, behind `authenticate` + `authorize('admin')` (which already lets `admin` and `super admin` both through, per the existing `authorize` middleware - satisfies "Admin and super admin see the same rows" with no extra code).
- **Testing an append-only table that spans the whole run, not just this stage:** `admin_audit_log` has no FK to `users`, so `truncateAll()` never clears it, and because `globalSetup` only resets the DB once per `vitest run` (not per file), rows from every earlier 26a/26b/26c test in the same run persist throughout. This isn't a new problem Stage 26d introduced, but it is the first stage where it actually matters, since `listAuditLogsPage`'s own tests need exact counts. Resolved by scoping every pagination/filter test's query by an `actor`/`target` username (or, for the "deleted user" test, by `action`+`reasonCode`) that only exists in the live `users` table for that test's duration - a stale row from an earlier, already-truncated test has a NULL joined username via the `LEFT JOIN` and can never match a substring filter on a currently-live username. Documented this reasoning in both new test files' headers so it doesn't need rediscovering later.
- Caught and fixed two precision bugs while writing the query-level tests myself, before they became real issues: (1) testing `from`/`to` inclusivity by reading back a `clock_timestamp()`-generated `created_at` and feeding it straight back as the bound failed, because node-postgres's `Date` truncates the column's microsecond precision, so the truncated bound could sit just before the row's real timestamp - fixed by inserting a test row with an explicit, millisecond-precision `created_at` (a plain `INSERT` with that column given no, since the append-only trigger only blocks `UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`TRUNCATE`, not `INSERT`); (2) a case-insensitivity test called the query function directly with an uppercase filter and failed, because lowercasing is the controller's job (`usernameSubstringSchema`), not the query's - fixed the test to pass pre-lowercased input at that layer, matching `listUsersPage`'s own convention of leaving case handling to the caller.
- Verification run: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint .` clean. New test files: `auditLog.queries.test.ts` (listAuditLogsPage additions) 18/18, `auditLog.controller.test.ts` (new) 18/18. Full suite: 914/914 clean on one run. An earlier full-suite run hit a native-module crash (`libc++abi: ... Napi::Error`) partway through that cascaded into unrelated failures in `races.concurrency.test.ts` and elsewhere (files this change never touched); re-ran clean immediately after, consistent with the environmental flakiness already logged in the 26a-26c entries, just a more disruptive manifestation of it this time.

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-opus-5-5)
