**Governing decision:** George's ECS Fargate plan, `ecs-fargate-session-prompt.md` ("Task: move FoC from Docker Compose to AWS ECS on Fargate, as a personal AWS practice project"), section "Phase 1: repo changes", items 1-11. The plan was supplied as a local file attachment and is not committed to this repository.

**Prompts (exact):**

> @"C:\Users\Aeodile\Downloads\ecs-fargate-session-prompt.md"
> The attached file, ecs-fargate-session-prompt.md, is my full plan for moving this repo from Docker Compose to AWS ECS on Fargate. Treat it as my instructions, including its ground rules, and don't reopen its decisions unless a fact proves one wrong.
>
> Start at its "First steps" section: confirm the current main commit and that 1fad383 is still reachable, tell me in a few lines how you'll begin, then start Phase 1 one change at a time.
>
> Note that the course restrictions in AGENTS.md can be considered less heavily, since all big decisions are already made and trying to force tiny decision is pedantic and waste of resources and time.

**Key responses:**

Built, per the plan's items:

- Items 1, 3: `DB_SSL` (default off) on user, credit and supplier, giving verified TLS on the connection pools.
- Item 4: RDS CA bundle added to the deploy stage of all four backend images at `/etc/ssl/rds-ap-southeast-1-bundle.pem`. URL verified: it returns three Amazon RDS `ap-southeast-1` root CAs.
- Item 5: `REDIS_TLS` (default off) at every Redis client. A search found no sites beyond the plan's list; `adapterPub.duplicate()` and order's queue dashboard inherit their options. Order gained one small options builder, `redisConnectionOptions`, used by its three sites.
- Item 6: `PHOTO_STORE_REGION` (default `us-east-1`); `forcePathStyle` kept.
- Item 7: static supplier `GET /health`, mounted ahead of the rate limiter.
- Item 8: `keepAliveTimeout` 65000 and `headersTimeout` 66000 on all four HTTP servers.
- Item 9: `supplier-service/Dockerfile.seed` with an allowlist `Dockerfile.seed.dockerignore`, so root `.env` files and JWT keys cannot enter the repo-root build context. `DB_SSL` and `PHOTO_STORE_REGION` passed through `vitest.seed.config.ts`.
- Item 10: new variables added to the four `.env.example` files.

Verification actually run:

- Unit tests: credit 147/147, order 638/638, supplier 429/429. User 829 passed and 26 failed; the same 26 failed before any change and no new failure appeared. They are Windows-only: `tests/config.test.ts` spawns `.bin/tsx` directly (25) and `tests/scripts/setupLocalDev.test.ts` asserts a Unix file mode (1). `tests/config.test.ts` could therefore not exercise the changed config on this machine; the new settings are covered by new separate tests. CI (Linux) was not run.
- Typecheck, lint and build passed where the services define them.
- Boot test (item 11): user, credit, supplier and order deploy images plus all three worker commands, on throwaway plain servers and again on throwaway TLS-only servers. All stayed up, with no error-looking log lines. `/health` returned 200 with `Keep-Alive: timeout=65` on all four, and credit fetched user's JWKS. `pg_stat_ssl` showed TLS 1.3, including `credit_app` for credit, whose grants still refused `DELETE` on `transaction_log`. Order applied its migrations through the image's default command with `sslmode=require`.
- TLS rejection tests: the credit pool, order app, supplier pool and all three Redis clients each connected with a valid certificate and were refused with an untrusted CA and with a certificate for another hostname. The user pool was tested with a valid certificate and an untrusted CA only; it uses the same `pg` options as credit.
- Plan item 2 (order SSL) results, tested locally against a TLS-only Postgres with `sslmode=require`. The app verified the certificate: it refused an untrusted CA and a wrong-hostname certificate. `prisma migrate deploy` encrypted without verifying: it succeeded with an untrusted CA, and with `sslmode=disable` the server refused it. The real RDS behaviour still needs confirming at first boot.
- Seed (item 9): two attempts failed because no photo store was running, after creating one supplier that has no photo in the seed data. It was then run twice in the image over verified TLS, using Adobe S3Mock as an S3 stand-in. The first created 13 suppliers and the second created 0. Rows and objects stayed at 14 suppliers, 10 photo rows and 10 objects, so it is safe to re-run with no orphaned photos. Four suppliers have no photo (one `.webp`, three files not found); the seed reports this by design. Real AWS S3 was not tested.
- Image checks: CA bundle readable by each image's user with `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` loading cleanly. No `.env`, key or `.pem` files in the seed image outside `node_modules`.
- JWT key command from the plan rehearsed with a throwaway keypair (1732 bytes): the service booted and no key text appeared in its logs.
- Shutdown with an init process: workers, credit and order exited 0 on SIGTERM within about a second. Supplier and user have no SIGTERM handler and exited 143.
- Not tested: anything on AWS, the frontend image, and `listen [::]:80` on Fargate.

Facts found while testing:

- `mysql2` only checks the certificate hostname when `verifyIdentity` is set; `rejectUnauthorized` alone does not, per its source. With the flag set, a wrong-hostname certificate was refused.
- `ADD --chmod=644` also applies to a parent directory that `ADD` creates, which made the file unreadable to order's `USER node`. Node only warned and continued without the CA. Fixed by placing the file directly in `/etc/ssl`.
- A `pg` connection to an IP address with a certificate for `localhost` was accepted in testing. A DNS host, which is what RDS endpoints are, was checked and refused on mismatch.
- `pg` prints a `SECURITY WARNING` at startup for `sslmode=require`, because it treats `require` as `verify-full` today and says this will change in a future major version.
- Norton Web/Mail Shield on the development PC re-signs direct TLS connections, so Redis TLS tests from the Windows host failed for every client, including a plain Node TLS client. The Redis tests were moved into a Docker network, where all three clients behaved correctly. Postgres and MySQL tests from the host were not affected, because their TLS starts inside the database protocol.
- `quay.io/minio/minio` and `quay.io/minio/mc` returned 401 on a fresh pull during this session.

## 2026-11-06 — ECS Fargate Phase 3: CD workflow

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-opus-5-5)
**Mode:** generate
**Scope:** Implementation code | Boilerplate
**Governing decision:** `docs/ecs-fargate-session-prompt.md`, "Phase 3: CD", plus George's chat decisions to run CD from the team repo and deploy on every merge to `main`.

**Prompts (exact):**

> this is intended, it should auto deploy on every main merge

The work started when George sent a screenshot of the IAM role's trust policy with no text, after the assistant had said it would write `deploy.yml` once that was confirmed. The rest of the brief is the plan section named above.

**Key responses:**

- `deploy.yml` builds and pushes 5 images on every push to the team repo's `main`, tagged with the git SHA for `linux/amd64`, then deploys 5 web services followed by 3 workers. A manual run offers build-only mode, a list of services, and an optional seed image build.
- `ecs-deploy.sh` fetches a service's current task definition, swaps only the image, registers it, updates the service and waits for it to settle.
- Implementation choices stated to George: a missing cluster or service skips the deploy with a notice and does not fail the run; a service at 0 tasks reports that nothing started; a rollback counts as a failed run; workers deploy after web services; the seed image builds only on manual request, tagged with the SHA and `latest`; provenance and SBOM manifests are turned off so the ECR rule counts builds.
- Verification run: 11 scenarios of `ecs-deploy.sh` against a fake AWS CLI in a local container, plus checks that the registered task definition keeps the command, env, secrets and `stopTimeout` and drops the read-only fields. `shellcheck` and `actionlint` were clean. The inputs used were found in the `action.yml` of the configure-aws-credentials, amazon-ecr-login and build-push actions at the pinned major versions.
- Not tested: the workflow has not run on GitHub, and nothing has run against real AWS.

## 2026-11-08 — Precise delivery location: design spec and implementation plan

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-sonnet-5-5)
**Mode:** docs
**Scope:** Requirements formatting
**Governing decision:** The team's chat answers of 2026-11-08, quoted below. No decision is written elsewhere yet; this spec is where they are first recorded.

**Prompts (exact):**

> in the current request flow, the deliver to is a dropdown with system defined locations mapped to specific IDs. I want to add a free text box below that for users to key in exact location details. I also want the user tables to store the last request's location, so that when a new request is made, there can be a little helper prompt asking if the user wants to reuse the same delivery details and a single click prefills the fields

> 1. free text will be a new column "deliveryDetails". notnull. max length 250 chars
> 2. a new table last_request will store "last_req_del_loc_id" (same as deliverLocationId of order db, integer) the and "last_req_del_loc_details" (same as deliveryDetails, free text, notnull, max 250 chars) these 2 fields will be used together to populate the request form if needed.
> 3. two new endpoints to the new table will be created for read and update, and when the user creates a request, that endpoint will be called to read the 2 values. On request submission, the update endpoint is used to update the values. editing an existing order also invokes the same update endpoint
> 4. where is order-service writing to user-service??
> 5. if the location id is no longer an option, the prompt will not be shown. shown only for new requests. the click prefills both the location id selector and the free text field

> 1. the user services onws the table and enpoints, as previously devided
> 2. the UUID will be the userid, just like the user_bookmarks table
> 3. both db level and api validation. deliveryDetails on requests is just the the last_req_del_lo_details
> 4. existing orders gets a "Nil". This is also the default
> 5. follow existing conventions used by the user_bookmarks flow
> 6. if the row does not exist (which should not happen), i should get a 200 with nulls so the flows dont get blokced, and upon successful request, the row will be populated
> 7. the authenticated user will only update their own row
> 8. the ids are populated from the form, which is already pulled from the actual db, so there is no need to do another round of validation.
> 9. yes, required field. this will be enforced on the frontend that prevents any extra chars after 250chars. if that is somehow bypassed , return 400 bad request
> 10. no error. they are async. if the order fails, the user will likely want to send the request again. then the stored values will act as a recovery as well.
>
> Also move all changes to a new branch "add precise delivery location". start with spec and plan

> 1. confirm
> 2. delivery details are compulsory
> 3. follow existing code name style and message text. empty and whitespace only values are gated on the frontend, and trailing spaces will be trimmed before storing to the db
> 4. parallel call. completely unrelated, and will go ahead even if the order is rejected. Rationale is as mentioned, for the record to serve as a "last state"
> 5. the delivery details will be displayed together with the existing deliveryLocatioId everywhere the id is used to retrieve the location name
> 6. the prompt will be a discrete "tips" card that is displayed below the deliver to form questions and above the choose a drop off point selector. prompt heading itself can be "Delivering to the same location?", with the body containing the rendered location and details, and a "Confirm" button
> 7. last_request is created on registration with the default "Nil" values. in the api call, receiving Nil is the same as there is no value, and the prompt will not even be rendered
> 8. ok yes, add an updated-at timestamp as well, just like the bookmarks

> 1. relax the last_req_del_loc_id to be nullable, and store null as the default
> 2. the update call is just sent together with the endpoint for updating the new last_request table. Trimming applies to leading spaces
> 3. the details will be displayed below the location name, they will exist as 1 entity and 1 field. Nil will be displayed as just Nil

**Key responses:**

- First turn: stopped and asked, under AGENTS.md §2.1, because the request needed schema and API decisions the docs did not record. Second turn: asked ten specific questions.
- Created branch `add-precise-delivery-location` (spaces are not valid in git branch names).
- Wrote the spec as a draft, recording the team's answers as decisions P1-P14. Items the answers did not settle are listed as open questions Q1-Q8 and were not filled in. The plan was not written, because it would depend on those answers.
- Second round: recorded the answers as P15-P20 in the spec. Endpoint names (`/users/me/last-request`) and the new error codes were named by the bookmark and error-code conventions and flagged for the team to check, because the reply to the endpoint question was "confirm". Three new gaps remain (Q1-Q3).
- Third round: recorded P21-P23 (nullable id, trimming and edit-time update, display), closed all open questions, and wrote the implementation plan. Existing users are not backfilled; this follows the team's "missing row reads as nulls, first update populates it" decision (P8) and is for the team to check.
- No code was changed. No tests were run.

Reuses the existing `requestOtp`/`checkOtp` (purpose `Admin Action`, which already existed in the DB enum and `OtpPurpose` type) for OTP send/verify/escalation/lockout isolation - no changes needed there, since that machinery is already generic over purpose. `resendAdminOtp` checks for a pending (unconsumed) `Admin Action` OTP row first, matching the existing Stage 12d pattern, before returning `NO_PENDING_OTP`. ## 2026-11-09 — System conversations

**Tool:** Codex (model: GPT-6)
**Mode:** generate, docs
**Scope:** Implementation code, Refactor/Docs
**Governing decision:** User-supplied final schema and contract in this conversation; implemented behavior recorded in chat-service/README.md, System conversations. Later prompts supersede earlier schema proposals.

**Prompts (exact):**

> Implement **system conversations** in the existing FoC chat service.
>
> ## Context
>
> Currently, chat conversations are tied to successfully created orders. However, some system notifications (e.g., failed scheduled order creation) have no associated order, so there is no conversation to deliver them to.
>
> The chat service already has a `POST /chat/send-system-notification` endpoint for internal microservices to send notifications.
>
> ## Requirements
>
> ### 1. System conversations
>
> Introduce a system conversation for each user.
>
> - A system conversation is identified by having `"SYSTEM"` as one of its participants.
> - Its participants should be `[userId, "SYSTEM"]`.
> - It must not be tied to an order (`orderId = null`).
> - Each user should have at most one system conversation.
> - System conversations should be created lazily when the first orderless notification arrives.
> - Subsequent notifications should reuse the existing system conversation.
> - System conversations are read-only: users cannot send messages to them.
>
> Prefer reusing the existing conversation and message models rather than introducing a separate notification model.
>
> Check the existing Prisma schema before implementation. If participants are constrained to UUIDs or user foreign keys, make the minimum necessary schema changes to support `"SYSTEM"` safely.
>
> ### 2. Update `POST /chat/send-system-notification`
>
> Preserve the existing endpoint contract and authentication.
>
> Modify the notification routing logic:
>
> - If the notification has a valid associated order, deliver it to the corresponding order conversation using the existing behaviour.
> - If the notification has no associated order, deliver it to the recipient's system conversation.
> - If the system conversation does not exist, create it automatically.
> - Do not silently fall back to a system conversation when an explicitly supplied order ID is invalid or its conversation is missing. Preserve or handle that error explicitly.
> - Do not create an order or an order conversation for orderless notifications.
>
> ### 3. Idempotency
>
> Preserve the existing message ID contract:
>
> - The calling microservice generates the message UUID.
> - Retries must reuse the same message UUID.
> - Duplicate requests must not create duplicate messages.
> - Concurrent requests must not create duplicate system conversations.
> - Use appropriate database constraints and atomic operations or transactions.
>
> ### 4. Socket.IO real-time updates
>
> Integrate system conversations with the existing Socket.IO implementation.
>
> The frontend already subscribes to:
>
> - `user:<userId>` for conversation list updates.
> - `chat:<conversationId>` for message updates.
>
> Ensure that:
>
> - Creating a system conversation notifies the recipient through their user room.
> - Sending a system notification updates the conversation list through the existing user-room event.
> - New messages are emitted to the corresponding conversation room.
> - Existing event names and payload formats are preserved wherever possible.
> - Socket room access is authenticated and restricted to the conversation's actual participants. `"SYSTEM"` is not a real user and must not be treated as an authenticated participant.
>
> ### 5. Conversation APIs
>
> Ensure existing conversation endpoints support system conversations:
>
> - Users can retrieve their own system conversation in their conversation list.
> - Users can retrieve messages from their system conversation.
> - System conversations do not require an order ID.
> - System conversations cannot be created through the normal user-facing conversation creation endpoint.
> - Users cannot send messages to system conversations.
> - Other users cannot access someone else's system conversation.
>
> Update any response DTOs or validation logic that currently assumes every conversation has an order.
>
> ### 6. Testing
>
> Add or update tests covering:
>
> - First orderless notification creates a system conversation.
> - Subsequent orderless notifications reuse it.
> - Different users receive separate system conversations.
> - Notifications with valid order IDs retain existing routing behaviour.
> - Invalid order IDs do not silently fall back.
> - Duplicate message UUIDs are idempotent.
> - Concurrent notifications cannot create duplicate system conversations.
> - Users cannot send messages to system conversations.
> - Users cannot access another user's system conversation.
> - Socket.IO events are emitted correctly.
>
> ## Implementation constraints
>
> 1. Inspect the existing chat-service architecture, Prisma schema, routes, controllers, services, authentication middleware, and Socket.IO implementation before making changes.
> 2. Follow the repository's existing conventions.
> 3. Minimise unnecessary changes and avoid breaking existing order conversations.
> 4. Preserve the existing `X-Service-Key` authentication for internal notification requests.
> 5. Preserve existing endpoint contracts where possible. Make the order ID optional only where appropriate.
> 6. Add a Prisma migration if the schema needs changing.
> 7. Do not introduce a separate notification service.
> 8. Do not modify unrelated microservices unless necessary.
>
> ## Deliverables
>
> Implement the changes directly in the repository, then provide:
>
> - A summary of files changed.
> - Any database schema changes and migration commands.
> - An explanation of the updated notification routing.
> - Any frontend changes required.
> - Test results and any remaining limitations.
>
> **Important:** Do not assume the current database structure or endpoint payloads. Inspect the actual implementation first and adapt the solution accordingly.

> orderless requests supply null!

> how about, instead of the participants saying "SYSTEM", determine if a chat is a system chat by checking if order id is null.
> before creating a system chat, check if user already has a conversation with null order id to make sure that system chat does not already exist

> participant role will also be null. then title is "FoC".

> 403 forbiddene

> oh okay sorry scrap that. i have a better idea. create a new table called `system_chats` with the following fields:
>
> - created_at
> - updated_at
> - user_id (unique)

> sorry add one more field for conversation_id. then the messages can link to the system_chats

> yepss

> primary key is conversation_id

> when it is a system message, supply null to order id and add a field for `recipient` with the userid

> ohh okay sorry wait i have another idea

> system chats still exist in conversations table with the order_id as null and title as "FoC". but there is another table "system_chats" with fields&#x20;
>

**Key responses:**
Inspected schema, routes, controllers, services, authentication, sockets and frontend. Asked for team schema/interface decisions before writing code. ## 2026-11-09 — order-service: Synchronous order creation and pending-order 409

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-opus-5-5)
**Mode:** generate | refactor
**Scope:** Implementation code
**Governing decision:** George in chat, 2026-11-09: order creation reserves credits synchronously with no retry, so the client learns the outcome in the response; a create while the requester has a `pending` order is rejected 409 with the message "Another order request is currently pending, please try again."; answers to the agent's questions (below) fix the status codes, the failed-row handling and the release on a transient failure.

**Prompts (exact):**

> no, continue working on this branch,
>
> remove the retry mechanism when an order is created, so its fully sync now,
> when creation fails, the client knows immediately
>
> and when an order in "pending" state exists, any requests to create an new order is rejected 409 conflict with message "Another order request is currently pending, please try again."

> (Agent questions) When the synchronous credit reserve succeeds, what should POST /orders return? / When the reserve fails, what happens to the order row and the response? / Which HTTP statuses for a failed reserve? / The 409 check: whose pending orders count?
> (Answers) 201 with the open order / Keep row as failed / 422 / 503 / Same requester only

> (Agent question) If credit-service is unreachable or returns 5xx, the reserve may still have gone through on its side. Today the worker then queues a credit release. Keep that?
> (Answer) Queue a release

**Key responses:**

- `createOrder` writes the order `pending`, calls credit-service `reserve` once (no retry), then moves the order to `open` (201 with the open order) or `failed` before answering. Refused by credit-service -> `failed`, 422 (`INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS` for `INSUFFICIENT_UNRESERVED_CREDITS`, otherwise new `CREDIT_RESERVE_REJECTED`), no release. Unreachable / 5xx -> `failed`, 503 `CREDIT_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, and a `credit_release` outbox row (the release still runs in the worker with its retries). Order events (`order:created` / `order:failed`) and the open order's `chat_create` task are still produced, through the existing `transitionOrder`.
- New `ORDER_PENDING_EXISTS` -> 409 with the given message, checked per requester inside the create transaction. Implementation choice made by the agent: a transaction-scoped Postgres advisory lock keyed on the requester id (`pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(requesterId))`) so two concurrent creates cannot both pass the check. No schema change.
- The worker's `credit_reserve` job (retry, retries-exhausted release, `RESERVE_RETRIES_EXHAUSTED`) is removed; a leftover reserve job now fails as an unknown task. The API now gets a credits client (`CREDIT_SERVICE_URL`, added to the order-service container in `compose.yaml`).
- Error messages reuse the existing order-service texts for `INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS` and `CREDIT_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`; `CREDIT_RESERVE_REJECTED` reads "Your credits could not be reserved. Please try again." (agent wording, modelled on the frontend's former generic text).
- Frontend `CreateRequest.jsx`: Post awaits the response and shows its message on failure; the socket wait and `/orders/mine` re-check are removed. `reserveFailureMessage` in `api/orders.js` is removed (no other users). `watchOrderEvents` in `realtime/orderSocket.js` is left in place, now unused by this page.
- Points raised for the team (not decided by the agent): `credits.client.ts` has no request timeout ("by decision"), so a hung credit-service call keeps the request open and the order `pending`, during which the requester gets 409; if the API process dies between writing the pending row and settling it, the order stays `pending` and blocks that requester's creates, with nothing that settles it (the worker's reserve job used to cover this). ECS task definitions are not in the repo, so `CREDIT_SERVICE_URL` must be added to the order-service API task by hand.

Verification: order-service `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` clean; `npm test` 18 files, 707 tests passed. The e2e suite (`test/credit-saga.e2e-spec.ts`, rewritten for the synchronous flow, with new sequential and concurrent pending-order tests) typechecks but was **not run**: no Postgres was available. Frontend `npm test`: 222 passed, 1 failed, the same pre-existing `CreateRequest.test.jsx` `maxLength` failure noted in the previous entry.

**Key responses:**

## 2026-11-09 — Scheduled Errands Stage 28 f: Worker

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-sonnet-5)
**Mode:** generate
**Scope:** Implementation code
**Governing decision:** instructions.md Stage 28, "Stage f: Worker"

**Prompts (exact):**

> read through instructions.md. i have finished up to 28e. let's start with f. dont forget the git workflow

**Key responses:**
Implemented `worker/series-worker.ts`: a 1-second BullMQ job scheduler (`startScheduledTask`,
same pattern as `release-redrive.ts`) that each tick claims every due series (`nextFireAt <= now`
OR `nextRetryAt <= now`, `updateMany`/`deleteMany` guarded by `version`) and runs instructions.md's
fire-time checks, retry, catch-up/skip and finished-series-deletion rules: user check
(`user.client.ts`'s `statusForWorker`), supplier/location/opening-hours check
(`suppliers.client.ts`'s worker methods from Stage c2), the "completeBy already past at fire
time" skip, the "one retry slot per series" (a due next occurrence drops a stale retry, writing
its own failed row), and "posted late" notes (> 1 minute after the scheduled time) added to the
order's chat once it opens. Posting an occurrence reuses `orders.service.ts`'s `createOrder`
request path, extracted into a new exported `createPendingOrderAndSettle` (same advisory lock,
same pending-order exclusivity, same synchronous reserve-then-settle; `createOrder` itself is
behaviourally unchanged) with a `seriesId` attached, per "each occurrence is created through
the normal create path."

The retry backoff (user/supplier-service-unreachable: up to 4 attempts, waits capped 1/2/4s
with full jitter) follows the "Stage 19 shape" instructions.md points to
(`user-service/src/services/email.service.ts`), but — since the scheduler must not block one
series while others are due — is persisted across ticks via the series row's own retry columns
rather than a blocking loop; the stage's 30s overall deadline has no dedicated timestamp column,
so it is satisfied structurally by the 4-attempt cap together with each call's own 3s timeout
and the 1/2/4s backoff caps (worst case well under 30s) rather than tracked directly. Notices:
one sent immediately on entering `user_service_unreachable`/`supplier_closed` retry (and again
on exhaustion/failure); `supplier_service_unreachable` sends only the exhaustion/failure notice,
per "notify only when exhausted." `SeriesFailureReason` (series.service.ts) gained the worker's
own reasons; `formatSgDateTime`, `DEFAULT_DURATION_MINUTES` and the failed-row/notice builder
(renamed `buildStoppedOccurrenceWrite`, now taking an explicit `scheduledAt` so the worker can
reuse it for occurrences that were never in retry) were exported from Stage e's
`series.service.ts` for this purpose, with no change to their existing callers' behaviour.

**Schema fix (stopped to ask the user):** Stage f's design requires `OrderSeries.nextFireAt` to
be nullable (null = no further occurrences, used to trigger the finished-series delete), but
Stage a's already-merged migration had created it `NOT NULL` — a discrepancy Stage e's own log
entry had already flagged but left unresolved. Asked the user how to proceed (new migration vs.
a NOT-NULL sentinel value); they chose a new migration. Added
`prisma/migrations/20261109130642_nextfireat_nullable` (`ALTER COLUMN "nextFireAt" DROP NOT
NULL`) and the matching `schema.prisma` change, then regenerated the Prisma client. Applied it
to the locally running dev stack's `order-db` (the only Postgres instance available in this
environment) rather than a disposable one, since reaching the already-running `order-db`
container required reusing its persisted volume; the running `order-service`/`order-worker`
containers were not restarted and stayed healthy throughout.

**Deviation (not one of instructions.md's listed outcomes):** a requester already having
another `pending` order at the exact moment a scheduled occurrence fires (an interaction with
George's 2026-11-09 synchronous-reserve + one-pending-order-at-a-time change, which postdates
this stage's text) is treated like any other post-time failure — failed row + notice, not
retried, reason `SERIES_PENDING_ORDER_CONFLICT` — since the series has already advanced past
that occurrence by the time posting is attempted. Flagged in the code and here for the team to
confirm.

**Verification:** `npx tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint --type-aware`, and the build (`tsc -p
tsconfig.build.json`) all clean. `npx vitest run` — 816/816 tests pass (25 files), including the
new `worker/series-worker.spec.ts` (18 tests: posting + the late-note threshold on both sides,
the completeBy-already-past skip, every fire-time-check failure/retry outcome (user
suspended/pending/not-found/locked, user- and supplier-service-unreachable entering and

suites after the `createPendingOrderAndSettle` extraction. `npm run db:migrate`'s underlying

## 2026-11-10 — Fix F3: isLocked uses the DB clock (convention 5)

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-fable-5-1)
**Mode:** refactor | generate
**Scope:** Implementation code | Refactor/Docs
**Governing decision:** the team's F3 fix note pasted in chat on 2026-11-10 (quoted below), implementing instructions.md "Conventions established in the code" item 5 (time comes from the database clock; compare against `clock_timestamp()`; no `Date.now()` outside JWT iat/exp)

**Prompts (exact):**

> dont forget the git workflow

> Fix F3: isLocked must use the DB clock (convention 5).
>
> - In every query whose row reaches toUserResponse (findUserById, listUsersPage,
>   the status/role/active-view/unlock UPDATE ... RETURNING paths, and any others —
>   grep for callers), select
>   (login_locked_until IS NOT NULL AND login_locked_until > clock_timestamp()) AS is_locked
>   For RETURNING, append it: RETURNING \*, (...) AS is_locked.
> - Use the same SQL expression for the `locked` filter in listUsersPage, so filter and
>   field cannot disagree. Factor it into one shared SQL fragment constant.
> - toUserResponse reads row.is_locked. Make is_locked a required field on the row type,
>   so a query that omits it fails to compile instead of returning undefined.
> - Remove Date.now() from userResponse.ts. Grep src/ for any other Date.now() use and
>   report each one (JWT iat/exp are the only allowed exception).
> - If the unlock service decides lock vs no-op from anything other than SQL, switch it to
>   the same expression, evaluated on the row it locks FOR UPDATE.
> - Test: backdate login_locked_until to 1 s in the future and 1 s in the past. Assert
>   isLocked and the locked=true|false filter agree in both cases, and that unlock on the
>   just-expired row is a no-op with no audit row.

**Key responses:**
Grepped for every `toUserResponse` caller: `users.service.ts` (listUsers via `listUsersPage`; getUserById via `findById`; changeUserStatus/changeUserRole no-op returns via `lockUserById` and real changes via `updateUserStatus`/`updateUserRole` RETURNING; unlockUser via `lockUserByIdWithNow` plus a synthesized post-unlock row) and `me.service.ts` (changeActiveView via `updateActiveView` RETURNING). `updateUsername`/`updateEmail` never reach the mapper and were left unchanged.

In `users.queries.ts`, added the exported `IS_LOCKED_SQL` constant (`(login_locked_until IS NOT NULL AND login_locked_until > clock_timestamp())`) and a private `IS_LOCKED_COLUMN` (`... AS is_locked`). `findById`, `findByIdWithNow`, `lockUserById`, `lockUserByIdWithNow`, `listUsersPage`'s SELECT, and the `updateUserStatus`/`updateUserRole`/`updateActiveView` RETURNING clauses all select it. `listUsersPage`'s `locked` filter now uses `IS_LOCKED_SQL` / `NOT IS_LOCKED_SQL` (replacing the two hand-written `NOW()` comparisons); `NOT (...)` is true for a NULL `login_locked_until` since `(false AND NULL)` is false in SQL.

Row type: added `UserRowWithLock = UserRow & { is_locked: boolean }` and made `UserRowWithNow` extend it; every query above returns `UserRowWithLock`. `toUserResponse` now takes `UserRowWithLock` and returns `isLocked: row.is_locked`; `Date.now()` is gone from `userResponse.ts`. Within-decision choice: `is_locked` is required on the type the mapper accepts rather than on `UserRow` itself, because `UserRow` is also the result type of `SELECT *`/`RETURNING *` queries that never reach the mapper (`createUser`, `findByUsername`, `findByEmail`, `findSuperAdmin`, `createSuperAdmin`, `updateUsername`, `updateEmail`, and the test helpers); putting `is_locked` on `UserRow` would have made those types claim a column they do not select. The compile-time guarantee asked for holds: passing a row from a query that omits `is_locked` to `toUserResponse` is a type error.

`unlockUser` now decides lock vs no-op from `locked.is_locked` on the row it locks FOR UPDATE (`lockUserByIdWithNow`), replacing the JS comparison of `login_locked_until` against `db_now`; the synthesized post-unlock row carries `is_locked: false`.

`Date.now()` report for `src/`: after this change the only remaining uses are two in `src/services/email.service.ts` (lines 220 and 241), which bound the SMTP retry loop's overall wall-clock deadline (elapsed time between send attempts). They are not JWT iat/exp and were not changed; they do not touch any persisted expiry or lock. Flagged for the team under Deviations.

Tests: extended `tests/helpers/db.ts`'s `setLoginLockState` with an optional `lockedUntilSecondsFromNow` (the lock end is now `clock_timestamp() + make_interval(secs => ...)`), and added a four-case describe "isLocked and the locked filter use the DB clock (fix F3)" to `tests/services/users.service.test.ts`: lock ending 1 s in the future (isLocked true, in locked=true, not in locked=false); lock ended 1 s ago (isLocked false, lockedUntil still set, in locked=false, not in locked=true); unlock on the just-expired row is a no-op (lock columns, failed-attempt count and updated_at unchanged, no audit row); unlock on the 1 s-future lock clears it and writes exactly one USER_UNLOCK row.

Verification: `tsc --noEmit` clean for `src/` and `tests/`. Vitest: the five lock-related files (users.service, users.controller, me.service, auth.service, lockout.concurrency) 288/288 passed, then the full user-service suite 38 files / 995 tests passed (the `Error: insert failed` and `SMTP down` stderr lines are from pre-existing forced-failure tests). `npm run lint` (eslint): no findings.
No requirements, architecture, schema, or API decisions were made by the AI tool.

**Files:**

- `user-service/src/db/queries/users.queries.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/src/services/userResponse.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/src/services/users.service.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/tests/helpers/db.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/tests/services/users.service.test.ts` (modified)

**Deviations / questions raised for the team:**

- `is_locked` was made required on the mapper's input type (`UserRowWithLock`) rather than on `UserRow` itself, for the reason given above. If the team wants it on `UserRow`, every `SELECT *`/`RETURNING *` query and the test helpers would need to select it too.
- Two `Date.now()` uses remain in `src/services/email.service.ts` (SMTP retry deadline). They are outside the JWT exception but also outside convention 5's stated scope (OTPs, refresh tokens, persisted expiries). Left as is for the team to decide.

Accepted all changes.

> - The translation model is called via a supplied TRANSLATION_LLM_KEY, with a simple system prompt asking to translate the supplied messages into <preferred language> if not already. all received messages will be supplied in a json format as key value pairs, and the output will be also in a json format of the reused keys, and the translated values will also be returned as a json. if the message was already in the preferred language, the returned value will just be fixed as "SAME"

> - The "Translate" option shown in the mockup for non preferred language messages will not invoke the tranlation LLM. It will only serve as a toggle back to the translated version

> are the conversation stored based on the user or the order?; new user-service col, and fetched when the message tab is launched; BullMQ on shared Redis; gemini key. are we even operating with an event driven architecture thus far in the messaging service? i was thinking when the model returns, the db gets updated and would that by default lead to the ui updating?

>

>

> 6. 1 changes things slightly
> 7. 1 changes this

A non null value will signal that we need an event in bullmq to prepare the translation in that language for that user
>

> 7. model id is just "gemini-3.1-flash-lite", stored as TRANSLATION_LLM_MODEL. this and TRANSLATION_LLM_KEY are new env vars in chat-service

**Key responses:**
Declined the SDK-vs-HTTP pros/cons and recommendation as prohibited architecture/design work (AGENTS.md §2.2) and asked for the team's choice; stopped to ask for unrecorded schema/interface decisions (§2.1) before writing code. After the decisions were given: added `translate_to` and `translated_messages` (Prisma schema + hand-written migration); `POST /chat/conversations/:conversationID/translation` (Bearer auth; 400/401/404/403/409 as the read endpoint; stores or clears `translate_to`, queues a backfill on enable); BullMQ queue on the shared Redis (prefix `queue:chat`, name `translation`, order-service's default retry options); a per-message job queued after commit for every active, non-sender participant with `translate_to` set (user messages and system notifications); a job processor that re-checks `translate_to` before spending anything, skips already-translated and own messages, batches 20 per Gemini call (`@google/genai`, `responseMimeType: application/json`), stores one row per message (including "SAME") and emits `message:translated`; `translatedContent` in `GET .../messages` scoped to the requester; `TRANSLATION_LLM_KEY` (required) and `TRANSLATION_LLM_MODEL` (default `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) env vars; user-service `users.preferred_lang VARCHAR(2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'en'`, `PUT /users/me/preferred-lang` (same shape as active-view, body `{preferredLang}`, subset en/zh/hi/ta/ms/es/ar) and `preferredLang` in user responses and `GET /users/me`.
Choices made within the delegated "follow existing convention" (for the team to confirm): the worker runs inside the chat-service API process (so it can emit through Socket.IO); SYSTEM messages with content are translated like TEXT; changing language while on deletes the user's stored translations for that chat before the backfill; the send response and `message:sent` payload are unchanged (no `translatedContent`); a failed enqueue is logged and does not fail the request (like broadcast failures).

## 2026-11-10 — Fix F4: unlockUser must not spread the full UserRow

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-fable-5-1)
**Mode:** refactor | generate
**Scope:** Implementation code | Refactor/Docs
**Governing decision:** the team's F4 fix note pasted in chat on 2026-11-10 (quoted below); the documented user response shape is instructions.md Stage 9 / Stage 15c (camelCase) / Stage 18d (`isLocked`, `lockedUntil`, `lockLevel`), as already encoded in `toUserResponse`

**Prompts (exact):**

> dont forget the git workflow

> Fix F4: unlockUser must not spread the full UserRow.
>
> - Define one shared constant in users.queries.ts listing the safe user columns (every
>   column toUserResponse needs, plus the lock columns and the is_locked expression from
>   F3), explicitly excluding password_hash. Use it for RETURNING / SELECT in user-facing
>   queries instead of `*` where the row ends up in a response.
> - unlockUser: keep the SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row internal, used only for the
>   lock-vs-no-op decision and the audit "before" value. Do the clears in an
>   UPDATE ... RETURNING <safe columns> and pass the returned row to toUserResponse.
>   No object spread, no hand-assigned reset fields.
> - Grep src/ for `...` spreads of user rows (`...user`, `...locked`, `...row`) and for
>   `SELECT *` / `RETURNING *` on users whose result reaches a response or a log. Report
>   each hit; fix any that carry password_hash outside a function that needs it
>   (login, password change/reset).
> - Test: for unlock (both the unlocked and no-op paths) and the other admin endpoints,
>   assert the response body's keys equal exactly the documented set, and that
>   JSON.stringify(body) contains neither "password_hash" nor "passwordHash".

**Key responses:**
Branched `fix/f4-unlock-safe-columns` off `main`.

`users.queries.ts`: added the exported `SAFE_USER_COLUMNS` constant (`id, username, email, created_at, updated_at, status, role, active_view, login_failed_attempts, login_failure_window_start, login_locked_until, login_lock_level, <IS_LOCKED_SQL> AS is_locked`; `password_hash` deliberately absent) and the `SafeUserRow` type (`Omit<UserRow, 'password_hash'> & { is_locked: boolean }`). `findById`, `listUsersPage`'s SELECT, and the `updateUserStatus` / `updateUserRole` / `updateActiveView` RETURNING clauses now use `SAFE_USER_COLUMNS` instead of `*` and return `SafeUserRow`. `resetLoginLock` now ends in `RETURNING ${SAFE_USER_COLUMNS}` and returns the cleared `SafeUserRow | null` (its other callers, login and the two password paths, ignore the return value and are unchanged). `toUserResponse` now takes `SafeUserRow`; `UserRowWithLock` (the FOR UPDATE reads) still satisfies it structurally, so the no-op paths of changeUserStatus/changeUserRole compile unchanged, and the mapper body is untouched.

`unlockUser`: the `lockUserByIdWithNow` row stays internal (lock-vs-no-op via `is_locked`, audit "before" value). The clears go through `resetLoginLock`, whose RETURNING row is passed straight to `toUserResponse`. The `{ ...locked, login_failed_attempts: 0, ... }` spread and its five hand-assigned fields are gone.

Within-decision choice: `findById` was also used by `me.service.ts`'s `initiateEmailChange` and `initiatePasswordChange` for a pre-lock `bcrypt.compare` against `user.password_hash`. Rather than leave `findById` selecting `*` for those two callers (which would have left the admin `GET /users/:id` path fetching the hash), added `findPasswordHashById` (selects only `password_hash`) and switched those two pre-lock reads to it. Their in-transaction re-check against `locked.password_hash` is unchanged.

Grep report (`src/`), spreads of user rows:

- `users.service.ts` unlockUser `...locked`: carried `password_hash` into the mapper's input object. **Fixed** (removed, see above).
- `users.queries.ts` listUsersPage `({ full_count, ...row }) => row`: now only ever sees `SAFE_USER_COLUMNS`, so it cannot carry the hash. Kept, with a comment.
- `auditLog.queries.ts:158` same `full_count` pattern on audit-log rows, not user rows. Not a hit.
  `SELECT *` / `RETURNING *` on `users`:
- `findById`, `listUsersPage`, `updateUserStatus`, `updateUserRole`, `updateActiveView`: results reach responses via `toUserResponse`. **Fixed** (safe columns).
- `lockUserById` / `lockUserByIdWithNow` (`SELECT * ... FOR UPDATE`): shared by login, refresh, the password/email change paths and the OTP services, which need `password_hash`; the admin no-op paths pass the row to `toUserResponse`, which copies only its listed fields. Kept; reported.
- `findByUsername` / `findByEmail`: login needs the hash; the other callers (register duplicate checks, me.service uniqueness checks, forgot-password/reset flows, bootstrap) use `id`/`status` only and never return or log the row. Kept; reported.
- `createUser` / `createSuperAdmin` (`RETURNING *`): callers use `.id` only; bootstrap's `console.log` prints the configured username, not the row. Kept; reported.
- `updateUsername` / `updateEmail` (`RETURNING *`): `changeUsername` returns `{ username, email }` picked from it; `updateEmail`'s result is unused. Kept; reported.
- `findSuperAdmin`: bootstrap existence check only. Kept; reported.
- `findByIdWithNow` (`SELECT *` + `db_now`): no longer has any caller in `src/` (its Stage 20 caller was replaced in Stage 26c); only `tests/db/queries/users.queries.test.ts` exercises it. Left in place; flagged under Deviations.
  Logs: no `console.*` call in `src/` prints a user row object.

Tests: `tests/controllers/users.controller.test.ts` gained `USER_RESPONSE_KEYS` + `expectExactUserResponse(body)` (keys sorted-equal to the documented set; `JSON.stringify(body)` contains neither `password_hash` nor `passwordHash`) and a describe "response bodies carry exactly the documented keys (fix F4)" covering POST unlock (locked → cleared, and non-locked no-op), PUT status (changed and no-op), PUT role (changed and no-op), GET /users/:id and every item of GET /users. `tests/db/queries/users.queries.test.ts`: `updatePasswordHash`'s test reads the hash via `findPasswordHashById`; the `listUsersPage` test that asserted rows _include_ `password_hash` now asserts the opposite; added a "safe user columns (fix F4)" block (constant names no `password_hash`; `findById` key set; `resetLoginLock` RETURNING row and null for unknown id).

Verification: `tsc --noEmit` clean for `src/` and `tests/`. `npm run lint` (eslint): no findings. Vitest: the five directly affected files 324/325 on the first run (the one failure was the pre-existing `listUsersPage ... including password_hash` assertion, then updated as above); first full run 1000/1002 with two failures in `tests/controllers/adminOtp.controller.test.ts` (`a regular user gets 403 FORBIDDEN`, `an invalid Elevated-Token does not block sending`) that passed 29/29 when that file ran alone and passed on the immediate full-suite rerun: 38 files / 1002 tests passed. Treated as a cross-file timing flake, not caused by this change. The `Error: insert failed` / `EMAIL_SEND_FAILED` stderr lines come from pre-existing forced-failure tests.
No requirements, architecture, schema, or API decisions were made by the AI tool.

**Files:**

- `user-service/src/db/queries/users.queries.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/src/services/userResponse.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/src/services/users.service.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/src/services/me.service.ts` (modified)

**Deviations / questions raised for the team:**

- Added `findPasswordHashById` so `findById` could drop `password_hash` without leaving the two me.service pre-lock bcrypt checks without a hash. If the team prefers no new query function, the alternative is to leave `findById` on `SELECT *` and only fix the RETURNING paths and the unlock spread.
- `findByIdWithNow` has no remaining caller in `src/`. Left as is; the team may want to remove it (and its test) separately.

## 2026-11-10 — Fix F2: ECONNRESET / "socket hang up" flake in the user-service test suite

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-fable-5-1)
**Mode:** debug | refactor
**Scope:** Debugging | Refactor/Docs (test code only, under `user-service/tests/`)
**Governing decision:** Team-authored fix note F2 pasted in chat (quoted below); Stage 7 ground rule 3 in `instructions.md` (no `src/` changes to make tests pass); `vitest.config.ts` (`fileParallelism: false`, unchanged).

**Prompts (exact):**

> don't forget the git workflow
>
> Fix finding F2 (Medium): reproducible ECONNRESET / "socket hang up" plus an unhandled rejection in the concurrency tests.
>
> Scope: test code only, under user-service/tests/. Do NOT modify anything in src/ (Stage 7 ground rule 3). If you find that a src/ change is needed, stop and report it as a separate finding instead.
>
> Context:
>
> - user-service/tests/concurrency/races.concurrency.test.ts uses `const post = (path) => request(app).post(path)` (line ~46), called in a tight 3-worker loop (lines ~251-257) with no error handling.
> - supertest starts and closes a new ephemeral server on every `request(app)` call. I suspect that under rapid concurrent calls this resets sockets (ECONNRESET / "socket hang up").
> - ai/usage-log.md reports the same failure signature in users.controller.test.ts and tests/concurrency/me.concurrency.test.ts under full-suite load, so treat this as systemic.
>
> Steps:
>
> 1. Read all three files, ai/usage-log.md and vitest.config.ts first. Reproduce the failure in races.concurrency.test.ts in isolation and show me the output before changing anything.
> 2. Confirm the root cause. Check whether the per-call ephemeral server is the cause. Also check whether the unhandled rejection comes from a worker promise that is never awaited or caught. Tell me what you find. Don't assume my hypothesis is right.
> 3. Fix it with the smallest change that addresses the confirmed cause. My expected approach:
>    - Create one `http.createServer(app)` listening on port 0 in `beforeAll`, close it in `afterAll`, and call `request(server)` so all requests share one listener.
>    - Collect worker results with `Promise.allSettled` and assert on them, so a transport error fails the test with a clear message and never becomes an unhandled rejection.
>    - If the same pattern appears in the other two files, put a shared helper in tests/concurrency/ (or tests/helpers/) and use it in all three. Don't duplicate the fix.
> 4. Do NOT add retry-on-ECONNRESET logic. It would mask real connection failures.
> 5. Do NOT weaken or remove any assertion, and do not change the number of workers or iterations.
> 6. Verify: run races.concurrency.test.ts in isolation at least 10 times in a row, then the full suite at least 3 times. Report pass/fail counts.
> 7. Don't touch vitest.config.ts unless the root cause requires it. If you think it does (for example fileParallelism is not false), explain why and ask first.
>
> AI-usage policy (CS3219 Appendix 2):
>
> - Add this header comment to every file you change or create:
>   // AI Assistance Disclosure:
>   // Tool: Claude Code (model: <your model>), date: 2026-11-09
>   // Scope: Debugged ECONNRESET flake in concurrency tests; replaced per-call supertest servers with a shared server and allSettled result handling.
>   // Author review: Reviewed, edited and tested by Gabriel.
> - Append an entry to ai/usage-log.md with a timestamp, this prompt, and a summary of the key response and changes.
>
> When done, give me a short summary: root cause confirmed or not, files changed, and the before/after run results.

**Key responses:**

Reproduction before any change (branch `fix/f2-concurrency-econnreset` off `main` after PR #186): `races.concurrency.test.ts` alone, 10 runs: 9 passed, 1 failed. The failure was _not_ a transport error: "refresh racing logout" got a 401 whose body had no `code` (`expected undefined to be 'INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN'`). One full-suite run: 1001/1002, the failure being `socket hang up` (`ECONNRESET`, `Socket.socketOnEnd`) in a plain sequential test in `auth.controller.test.ts`, i.e. not in a concurrency file at all.

Root cause investigation, and the user's hypothesis was not confirmed as stated:

- Hammering the per-call `request(app)` pattern with 3 workers × 400 refresh requests (a throwaway test, deleted) produced 0 anomalies, and so did a shared server. Rapid per-call server creation on its own does not reset sockets.
- supertest 7.3.0 creates `http.createServer(app)` per `request(app)` call and runs `listen(0)` on the wildcard address (`::`), closing it after the one request; superagent uses `agent: false`, so no keep-alive reuse is involved.
- Every 401 the app can emit carries a `code`, so a 401 without one did not come from the app. The "socket hang up" is a clean server-side FIN with no response, which a supertest server never does to its own single connection.
- Confirmed mechanism (macOS, Node 22.15.0): a wildcard `listen(0)` can be handed a port that another process already holds on `127.0.0.1`, because libuv sets `SO_REUSEADDR` and the kernel then skips the conflict when the bind addresses differ. The loopback client's connection then goes to the _other_ process. A throwaway script (`portcollide.mjs`, not committed) did 40,000 wildcard `listen(0)` calls: 6 of them returned a port held by one of three VS Code helper processes listening on `127.0.0.1` in the ephemeral range, and probing those ports got back that process's own `401 Unauthorized` text body, a `401` JSON body and a `404` HTML page, exactly the "401 with no code" seen in the isolated repro; a process that drops the connection instead yields the `socket hang up`. With 3 such ports in a 16,384-port range the odds are about 1 in 5,500 per request, which matches the observed 0–2 failures per full suite (several thousand requests) and roughly 1 in 10 isolated runs of a ~500-request file. The same script binding explicitly to `127.0.0.1`: 40,000 listens, 0 collisions, because the kernel then sees the exact conflict and skips the port.
- The per-call ephemeral server is therefore the _amplifier_ (one dice roll per request), not the direct cause; the root cause is the wildcard bind.
- Unhandled rejection: confirmed by code reading and a standalone demo. In the two `while (running)` worker loops the worker promises were created and only awaited ~250 ms later with `Promise.all(workers)`; a worker that throws in that window is reported by Node as an unhandled rejection (then "handled asynchronously"). Attaching `Promise.allSettled` at creation time yields 0 unhandled-rejection events and still surfaces both failures.

Fix (test code only, no `src/`, `vitest.config.ts` untouched since `fileParallelism` is already `false`):

- New `tests/helpers/server.ts`: starts one `http.createServer(app)` on `127.0.0.1:0` in a `beforeAll` registered at import time, closes it in `afterAll`, and exports `api()` as a drop-in for `request(app)` (returns `request(server)`).
- Replaced every `request(app)` call site with `api()` and dropped the now-unused `supertest`/`app` imports. This was widened beyond the three files named in the prompt: `tests/helpers/fixtures.ts` had to move too (the concurrency tests do most of their HTTP through `loginUser`/`createActiveUser`), and the remaining ten test files were migrated because the baseline full-suite failure was in `auth.controller.test.ts`, and every remaining per-request wildcard listen keeps the same per-request odds. No test logic, assertions, worker counts or iteration counts changed. No retry logic added.
- `races.concurrency.test.ts`: the two worker groups are now `Promise.allSettled(...)` collected at start, and a small `expectAllFulfilled()` fails the test with the worker's error message if any worker rejected.
- Header note: the prompt asked for `date: 2026-11-09` and `Author review: Reviewed, edited and tested by Gabriel.` Headers use the actual date (2026-11-10) and leave `Author review` blank, per AGENTS.md §4.1 (the agent never signs the review); the author fills it in.

Verification: `npx tsc -p tests/tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean; `npx eslint tests` clean. After the fix: `races.concurrency.test.ts` alone, 10 consecutive runs, 10 passed / 0 failed; full suite 3 consecutive runs, 3 passed / 0 failed (38 files, 1002 tests each). Before the fix, the same measurements were 9/10 and 1 failure in the single full run. The two stderr stack traces in the full-suite output come from pre-existing forced-failure tests and appeared identically in the baseline run.
No requirements, architecture, schema, or API decisions were made by the AI tool.

## 2026-11-10 — Stage 31e: Tests (Vitest)

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-sonnet-5)
**Mode:** generate
**Scope:** Implementation code (tests)
**Governing decision:** instructions.md Stage 31e ("Follow the Stage 7 ground rules and the Stage 19 mocking policy... Every Verification bullet in 31a-31d that does not need Docker or a real browser is a required test case.")

**Prompts (exact):**

> let's work on stage 31. don't forget the git workflow.
> done. we can do one PR. let's start with the next stage.
> go for 3c
> once done start 31d
> on with e

**Key responses:**

- Awaiting the fire-and-forget unlock-email send deterministically, without changing production behaviour: `triggerUnlockEmail` (auth.service.ts) calls `sendUnlockEmail(...).catch(() => {})` without awaiting it, so the caller's own promise (a supertest response, or authService.login's rejection) can settle before the mocked send does. The call to the mock itself, though, happens synchronously - `sendUnlockEmail(...)` is invoked, and `.catch()` attached, entirely before `triggerUnlockEmail` returns, which is itself before the HTTP response is written. So by the time the triggering request/call has resolved, the mock's call and the Promise it returned are already recorded in `sendUnlockEmailMock.mock.results`. Added `awaitLastUnlockEmail()` (`tests/helpers/email.ts`) which just reads and awaits that already-captured promise (`mock.results.at(-1)`). No change to any production file, no polling, no fake timers - it is reading a result that already exists by the time the test calls it.
- `tests/helpers/keys.ts` / `tests/utils/jwt.test.ts` (Stage 31a): added `signUnlockToken` (mirrors `signElevationToken`). Extended `verifyAccessToken`/`verifyElevationToken`'s existing cross-type-rejection tests with the new `ul+JWT` case, and added `signUnlockToken`/`verifyUnlockToken` describe blocks covering claim shape (`sub`/`iat`/`exp`/`lck`), the 1 hour expiry, and every cross-type/expired/tampered/wrong-key rejection, mirroring the existing elevation-token coverage.
- `tests/helpers/email.ts` / `tests/services/email.service.test.ts` (Stage 31b): added `sendUnlockEmailMock`, `unlockEmailCallsFor`, `latestUnlockUrlFor`, `awaitLastUnlockEmail` (global mock already added in setupFiles.ts for 31b). Added a `sendUnlockEmail` describe block covering subject/link content, the "too many failed attempts" wording with no lock-length/OTP/password text, the dev-fallback `[DEV EMAIL] ... url=...` line, and the `[OTP EMAIL] ... purpose=account_unlock ...` log line - the last two prove it goes through the shared `sendMailWithRetry`/`PURPOSE_COPY`-free path rather than a copy. Did not re-test the full transient/non-transient/backoff/deadline matrix for `sendUnlockEmail` purpose-by-purpose, since that logic is generic and already covered by the `sendOtpEmail` retry describe block above it (same principle `me.service.test.ts`'s own header comment states for not duplicating generic OTP logic per call site); one transient-failure case is included only to demonstrate the retry path is actually taken.

> for the frontend for the credit activity segment, help me add the value held, returned ... etc similar to the allocation +20 there.
>
> and to confirm this page has pagination right? for how many errand per page may i confirm? and is there lazy loading?

> ok rebuild it

> ok now commit the changes

**Key responses:**

_The change._ `Delta` in `frontend/src/pages/Wallet.jsx` rendered the bare word `held` or `returned` for `reservation` and `release`, while an allocation rendered `+20` and a transfer `+4` / `−4`. The amount was already a prop, so the branch now renders it before the label: `4 held`, `20 returned`, with the figure as `tnum font-medium text-ink-70` and the label left at `text-ink-40`.

_No sign on those two types._ A reservation moves credits from unreserved to reserved and a release moves them back; neither changes `total_balance`, which is why `describe()` in `frontend/src/api/credits.js` returns `delta: 0` for both. A `+` or `−` would read as a balance movement that does not reconcile against the total, so the figure is unsigned. `describe()` was not changed.

_Questions answered from the code, not changed._ The history is server-side keyset pagination at **20 transactions per page** (`TRANSACTION_PAGE_SIZE` in credit-service, ordered `created_at DESC, transaction_id DESC`, opaque base64url cursor, `nextCursor` null on the last page). That is 20 transactions rather than 20 errands: one errand normally produces a `reservation` plus either a `transfer` or a `release`. Loading is **infinite scroll**, not numbered pages — an `IntersectionObserver` on a sentinel below the list calls `loadPage(cursor)`, appends, and stops when `nextCursor` is null, with an `inFlight` ref guarding against a double fire.

**Verification actually run:**

- `npm run lint`: exit 0. The only warnings are the pre-existing ones in `src/pages/AdminUsers.jsx`; none in `Wallet.jsx`.
- `npm run build`: exit 0, `dist/assets/index-B7TR23Od.js`, 504.80 kB / 147.04 kB gzipped.
- `npm test`: **40 files, 298 tests, all passing.** There is no test covering `Delta`, so the suite proves no regression rather than proving this behaviour.
- `docker compose up -d --build frontend`: rebuilt, healthy in about 3 s, serving on 5173. Confirmed the container serves the new bundle — same hash as the local build — and that the minified output contains the new branch: `className:"w-20 shrink-0 text-right text-sm text-ink-40", children:[span{className:"tnum font-medium text-ink-70", children:n}, " ", e==="hold"?"held":"returned"]`.

**Files:**

- `frontend/src/pages/Wallet.jsx` (modified: `Delta`, plus the dated disclosure entry)
- `ai/usage-log.md` (modified)
- `README.md` (modified: Log index row)

**Deviations / questions raised for the team:**

1. **There is a second, near-duplicate `Delta` in the built bundle that was not changed.** It appears minified as `className:"tnum text-sm text-ink-40"` with no `w-20 shrink-0` and no amount, so it still renders the word alone. Only `frontend/src/pages/Wallet.jsx` was edited; the other copy is most likely `foc-mockup`'s version of the page or another component rendering credit rows. Flagged rather than hunted down, because it was outside what was asked for. `grep -rn "'held'" frontend/src foc-mockup/src` locates it.
2. **The transaction-type filter is client-side only** and was left alone. `const shown = rows.filter((t) => filter === 'All' || t.type === filter)` filters the rows already loaded and does not request more matching rows, so selecting "Transfer" on a long history shows only the transfers among the pages scrolled so far, presented as if complete. Making it server-side would need a `?type=` parameter on `GET /credits/transactions`, which does not exist — a new API surface, and the team's decision rather than the agent's.
3. **No test was added.** There is no existing test for `Delta` or for the Wallet list rendering, and the brief did not ask for one. A render test asserting `4 held` and the absence of a sign would be cheap if wanted.
4. **Committed on `docs/author-review-attributions`**, which is a documentation branch, because the author asked to stay on it. This is the only source change on that branch.

So the worker should exit at startup under `docker compose up`. The `supplier-service` block in the same file already sets it as `SUPPLIER_ORDER_SERVICE_API_KEY: ${SUPPLIER_ORDER_SERVICE_API_KEY:?set SUPPLIER_ORDER_SERVICE_API_KEY in .env}`.

## 2026-11-10 — Fix login redirect to register page after visiting Register then Log in

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-sonnet-5)
**Mode:** debug, generate
**Scope:** Debugging, Implementation code
**Governing decision:** Bug fix to existing login/redirect behavior; no new requirements, schema, or API decisions. Implements the existing intent of `frontend/src/pages/Login.jsx`'s post-login redirect (go back to where the user came from) by excluding auth pages from being a valid "from" target.

**Prompts (exact):**

> bug! before logging in, when i click "register" then "login", then i login, i login successfully, but it goes to the "create your account" page.i can go to suppliers and errands normally
>
> help me find out what could have caused it
>
> go for it

**Key responses:**
Traced the bug: the nav's "Log in" button calls `AuthContext.requireAuth`/`goToLogin`, which captures the _current_ page via `useLocation()` as `location.state.from`. If the user is on `/register` when they click "Log in," `/register` gets stored as `from`, and `Login.jsx`'s post-login `navigate(location.state?.from ?? '/', { replace: true })` then sends them back to `/register` instead of home. Fixed by checking whether `from`'s pathname is `/login` or `/register` and falling back to `/` in that case, in `frontend/src/pages/Login.jsx`. Verified: full frontend suite (305 tests, 40 files) passed after the change.

**Files:**

- `frontend/src/pages/Login.jsx` (modified)
- `ai/usage-log.md` (this entry)

## 2026-11-10 — Fix: ResendButton countdown not shown on first successful resend

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-sonnet-5)
**Mode:** debug
**Scope:** Debugging
**Governing decision:** N/A — pure bug fix to existing behaviour; no new schema/API/design decision. DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS (60) was already defined in ResendButton.jsx and already matched the server's configured OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS.

**Prompts (exact):**

> read only for now
>
> when i click resend, it registers, then when i click again, it shows resend in 28s - i want it to immedaitely show resend in xxxs

**Key responses:**
Traced the bug to `frontend/src/components/ResendButton.jsx` `handleClick`: `setCooldown(...)` was only called in the `catch` branch when the server rejected a resend with `OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN`. A successful first resend returns `{ message, code: 'OTP_SENT' }` with no retryAfterSeconds, so `cooldown` stayed at 0 and the button re-enabled immediately; only the second click (hitting the server's live cooldown) ever set the countdown. Confirmed via the backend handler (`user-service/src/controllers/auth.controller.ts` `resendOtp`) that the 200 response never carries a cooldown value, and that the server-side cooldown is `OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` = 60 in all checked-in env files, matching the component's existing `DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` constant. Fix: call `setCooldown(DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS)` immediately after a successful `onResend()`, so the countdown starts on the first click. No new UI copy, schema, or API change. Verification: not run (no dev server/tests executed in this session); needs manual check in the Register/ForgotPassword/Account/ElevationOtpModal resend flows.

## 2026-11-10 — Fix: pending-account OTP verification could be redirected to a different account

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-sonnet-5)
**Mode:** debug, generate
**Scope:** Debugging, Implementation code
**Governing decision:** Bug report plus follow-up decisions made by the user in this conversation (the original prompt's `<FILL IN: ...>` placeholder and the follow-on scope questions it raised), recorded here since no prior doc covered this case:

- Mechanism: login (on hitting the pending-account case) and register both issue a short-lived `pendingToken` httpOnly cookie (same base options as the existing `refreshToken` cookie) identifying the account; verify-otp/resend-otp (registration purpose only) must cross-check the submitted `email` against that cookie's account before any OTP-related logic runs.
- Token TTL = `config.otp.ttlMinutes` (same window as the registration OTP itself).
- Mismatch, missing, or invalid/expired cookie all produce the same `403 EMAIL_MISMATCH` response, with no distinction between the three cases, and none of them touch the OTP attempt counter, resend cooldown, or resend count.
- `forgot_password` purpose on the same two endpoints is intentionally unauthenticated and was left untouched.

**Prompts (exact):**

> Debugging task in user-service (CS3219 FoC). Follow the course AI usage policy:
> help with debugging and implementation only, don't make design decisions, add the
> AI attribution header at the top of every file you change, and give me the exact
> prompt and key output to paste into /ai/usage-log.md.
>
> Bug: pending-account verification can be redirected to a different account.
> Repro: two accounts, A and B, both in pending state. Log in as A by username.
> The app then asks for an email. If I enter B's email, I can verify account B
> (and I can use B's OTP) while holding A's login.
>
> Expected: the account being verified must always be the one identified at login.
> The email entered at the prompt must not choose the target account.
>
> Steps:
>
> 1. Find the login path for pending accounts and what credential (token/session)
>    it issues. Find the verify and resend-OTP handlers. Report which one takes the
>    account from the request body, and whether OTP sending also uses the submitted
>    email instead of the stored one. Show me the relevant code before changing anything.
> 2. Fix it so the handlers derive the account only from the credential issued at
>    login. On an email mismatch, behave as follows (my decision): <FILL IN: status
>    code, error code, whether it counts toward OTP/lockout limits, what the response
>    reveals>.
> 3. Check the other flows that take an email or username in the body (resend OTP,
>    admin elevation OTP, unlock) for the same pattern and list them. Don't change
>    them without asking me.
> 4. Add tests: (a) A's credential + B's email is rejected and B's status is
>    unchanged; (b) A's credential + B's email + B's valid OTP is rejected;
>    (c) the normal flow for A still works.
> 5. Run the test suite and report results.
>
> Keep changes minimal and don't touch unrelated code.

Follow-up decisions, collected via clarifying questions after the investigation showed pending-account login issues no credential at all today (so "the credential issued at login" did not yet exist to derive from):

> [Q] How should the server tie "the account identified at login" to verify/resend-OTP, given pending-account login issues no token today? [A] Short-lived pending token.
> [Q] On a mismatch, what should the response reveal and should it count toward OTP/lockout limits? [A] Email-keying comes before OTP, so it shouldn't be counted together.
> [Q] Given that, how should a mismatch be handled? [A] Reject before the OTP check, with a distinct error code, and no counter at all.
> [Q] Should register also set the pendingToken cookie, so the normal register → verify-otp flow (no login in between) keeps working? [A] Yes, register also sets the pendingToken cookie.
> [Q] If verify-otp/resend-otp is called with no pendingToken cookie at all, what should happen? [A] Same 403 EMAIL_MISMATCH as a real mismatch.
> [Q] How should the pending token travel between login/register and verify/resend-otp? [A] httpOnly cookie, like the refresh token.
> [Q] What HTTP status + error code should the mismatch use? [A] 403 EMAIL_MISMATCH.
> [Q] How long should the pending token stay valid? [A] Same as the current OTP expiry window.

**Key responses:**
Investigation (step 1): pending-account login throws `403 ACCOUNT_NOT_VERIFIED` before any token is issued (`auth.service.ts` `login()`), so there was no existing credential to derive from. `/auth/verify-otp` and `/auth/resend-otp` are public, unauthenticated endpoints that resolve the target account purely from the request body's `email` via `userQueries.findByEmail`. All other endpoints combining a body email/username with an auth credential (`me.controller.ts`, admin-elevation OTP) already derive the account from the credential, never the body — those were left alone, as instructed.

Fix: added a `signPendingVerificationToken`/`verifyPendingVerificationToken` JWT pair (`src/utils/jwt.ts`, header `typ: pv+JWT`, TTL `config.otp.ttlMinutes`); extended `AppError` with an optional `cookie` field so a thrown error can carry a `Set-Cookie` through the central error middleware (`src/app.ts`); `register()` and the pending branch of `login()` (`src/services/auth.service.ts`) now issue a `pendingToken` httpOnly cookie for the account; `verifyRegistrationOtp`/`resendRegistrationOtp` now reject with `403 EMAIL_MISMATCH` (via a shared `assertPendingTokenMatches` check, run before any OTP attempt/cooldown/count logic) if the cookie is missing, invalid, or names a different account than the submitted email; `auth.controller.ts` wires the cookie through for the registration-purpose branches only and clears it on successful verification. `forgot_password` branches of both endpoints are untouched.

Tests: added cases for A's token + B's email/OTP (rejected, B unchanged), no cookie at all (rejected), and confirmed A's own flow still succeeds, for both verify-otp and resend-otp; updated existing registration-purpose tests and test helpers (`tests/helpers/fixtures.ts`, `tests/services/auth.service.test.ts`, the two concurrency test files) to carry the new cookie through, since register/verify/resend's contracts changed. `forgot_password` test blocks were not touched.

Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx vitest run` — 1061 passed, 0 failed, 38/38 test files.

**Files:**

- `user-service/src/utils/jwt.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/src/utils/AppError.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/src/app.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/src/services/auth.service.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/src/controllers/auth.controller.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/tests/helpers/fixtures.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/tests/controllers/auth.controller.test.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/tests/services/auth.service.test.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/tests/concurrency/lock-recheck.concurrency.test.ts` (modified)
- `user-service/tests/concurrency/races.concurrency.test.ts` (modified)

**Deviations / questions raised for the team:**
The spec only named `tests/controllers/auth.controller.test.ts` for test updates; making the suite pass also required the same `pendingToken` plumbing in `tests/services/auth.service.test.ts` and the two concurrency test files, since they call the now-stricter service/HTTP functions directly for the registration purpose. This is mechanical fallout from the already-decided contract change, not a new decision, but is flagged here since it wasn't explicitly named upfront.

## 2026-11-10 — Bug fix: Manage users page scrolls horizontally on mobile

**Tool:** Claude Code (model: claude-sonnet-5)
**Mode:** debug
**Scope:** Debugging
**Governing decision:** N/A — mobile-viewport CSS bug fix, no requirements/architecture/schema/API decision involved; reported directly by the user with an iPhone-width screenshot of /admin/users.

**Prompts (exact):**

> this is the manage users page on iphone dimensions - help me resolve this (using git workflow e.g. PR)
> [attached screenshot of AdminUsers page clipped on a narrow viewport]

**Key responses:**
Root cause: `App.jsx`'s `<main className="flex-1">` is a flex item inside a `flex min-h-screen flex-col` container. Without `min-w-0`, a flex item's default `min-width: auto` lets its content (here, AdminUsers.jsx's table, which has `min-w-[720px]` inside an `overflow-x-auto` wrapper) stretch the flex item itself, so the whole page scrolled horizontally instead of just the table's own scroll wrapper. Fix: added `min-w-0` to `<main>` (`frontend/src/App.jsx`), a one-line class change; no change to AdminUsers.jsx or any other page was needed.
Verification: dev server start and any available build/lint/test checks run via a verification subagent; manual login-gated visual check of /admin/users on a simulated iPhone width was not performed in this session.
